data.description:
## Problem statement

When `implement.py finish` cannot fast-forward the main checkout to the commit it is
about to push (main checkout dirty from concurrent work), it logs a warning and pushes
anyway from that stale checkout. The `dev`/`main` push then runs `.githooks/pre-push`
with `--project-root <main checkout>` — so the full suite is measured against the *old*
working tree, and the result is cached under the *old* git-state fingerprint
(`HEAD` + dirty content). The push returns green in seconds without the pushed commit
ever being verified: a silent fail-open in the only full-suite enforcement point for
`dev`.

## Users

- **Agent implementers** running `implement.py finish` in a repo with a busy main
  checkout: they need a push that is either genuinely verified or loudly refused, never
  a green gate that proves nothing.
- **Producers / release reviewers** relying on `run_tests.py --summary` as the
  "the pushed commit was full-suite green" evidence trail.
- Example story: *As a producer reviewing a `dev` push, I want a green gate to mean the
  pushed commit's tree passed the full suite, so that I can trust `dev` without
  re-running the suite manually.*

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — fail closed on a stale checkout.** For a push targeting `refs/heads/dev` or `refs/heads/main`, the hook compares the gated `local_sha` (already on stdin) with the `HEAD` of the tree it is about to measure; on mismatch it **refuses the push before the suite runs**, and the message names the pushed commit, the checked-out `HEAD`, the tree path and the recovery steps. It never reports green using evidence from a different tree.
- **AC2 — fail closed on a dirty tree.** When `HEAD` matches the pushed commit but the tree has uncommitted/untracked changes, the gate also refuses (project-declared expected-dirty paths, if any, are excluded) — a dirty fingerprint can never equal the pushed commit's clean fingerprint, so a green run there is not evidence about the pushed commit.
- **AC3 — evidence at the pushed commit.** A green `dev` push from a clean checkout at the pushed commit still leaves a full-suite cache entry keyed to that commit (`run_tests.py --summary` reports it), i.e. the guard adds a precondition, not a different cache key.
- **AC4 — regression test.** `tests/test_git_hooks.py` reproduces "dirty main checkout / skipped fast-forward" (pushed `local_sha` ≠ checkout `HEAD`, and separately a dirty tree at the matching `local_sha`) in the existing hermetic sandbox, asserting the push is refused, both SHAs appear in the message, and the runner is **never invoked**; the existing green `dev`-push and feature-branch-skip tests still pass.
- **AC5 — documentation.** `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` documents the pushed-commit contract, the refusal conditions and messages, the recovery path, a copy-pasteable reproduction (mismatched-sha simulation), and that `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` / `--no-verify` remain the explicit escape hatches.
- At least one test/validation criterion is covered by the repo suite; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope decided (Q1 = A): repo-local only.** The change lands in this repository —
  `.githooks/pre-push`, `tests/test_git_hooks.py`, `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`. No
  agent-infrastructure file is edited: `implement.py` (Step 5/6), `test_cache.py` and the
  canonical hook copies in `projects/SorraAgents` are **out of scope** and are recorded as
  a framework follow-up (see *Related work*). Because the hook runs for every `dev` push,
  the fail-closed guard fixes the observable defect for this repo without touching the
  framework.
- `.githooks/pre-push` must stay POSIX `sh` with no new runtime dependencies.
- **Q3 = B (strict):** both a `HEAD` ≠ `local_sha` mismatch and a dirty tree at the
  matching commit refuse the push; the escape hatches (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`,
  `--no-verify`) keep working unchanged.
- Feature-branch pushes must keep skipping the suite (fast loop unchanged) — the guard
  applies only to `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/heads/main` targets.
- Cache plumbing stays fail-soft: mirroring must never decide a push's outcome.
- **Q2 = B (keep both items, one implementation):** this item and
  LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 (non-fast-forward retry path) share the *same* hook guard.
  Whichever is scheduled first implements the guard; the other becomes verification of
  its own trigger scenario only. No second copy of the guard.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` already reads all four stdin fields per pushed ref
  (`local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha`) but uses only `remote_ref`; `local_sha`
  is discarded, so the gate cannot tell which commit it is supposed to verify.
- The gate runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`
  with `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — i.e. the checkout `git push`
  runs in, which `implement.py finish` makes the **main checkout**.
- `test_cache.compute_git_state()` fingerprints `HEAD` + the content of every dirty path,
  so a stale-but-dirty main checkout produces a *valid, different* fingerprint; a
  previous green run for that same stale+dirty state is a legitimate cache hit → the gate
  returns green in seconds.
- `implement.py` Step 5 fast-forwards the main checkout's `dev` to the new commit
  precisely so the hook sees the new files; on failure it only logs
  `"Fast-forward dev failed (%s); push will proceed from the stale checkout — the
  context-budget gate may reject the push."` and continues to Step 6
  (`git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)`).
- The push path can also retry after a non-fast-forward rebase
  (`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`), which pushes the rebased commit from the main
  checkout — the guarded condition is identical, which is why LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 and
  this item share one implementation.
- Observed 2026-10-28 (LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND): main checkout dirty (8 unrelated paths),
  fast-forward skipped, main `dev` stayed at `7393ef14`, push landed `11870e99`; gate
  green in seconds; `run_tests.py --summary` reported `missing` for the pushed commit;
  a throwaway worktree at the pushed commit gave 6136 passed / 0 failed.
- Existing coverage: `tests/test_git_hooks.py` (13 hermetic sandbox tests, fake runner,
  behavioural assertions) — its `_hook()` helper always sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`, so
  no test can express "pushed commit ≠ checked-out tree"; `--strict-git-env` runs are
  driven through the fake runner, so the new tests need no real suite.

## Desired change

Add a **fail-closed pushed-commit guard** to the `dev`/`main` gate in
`.githooks/pre-push`:

1. While reading stdin, capture the `local_sha` of every gated ref
   (`refs/heads/dev|main`), ignoring deletion pushes (all-zero sha).
2. Before running the suite, resolve the gate tree (`repo_root`) and compare its
   `git rev-parse HEAD` with the captured `local_sha`. On mismatch → refuse with an
   actionable message (pushed sha, checkout `HEAD`, tree path, "re-run
   `implement.py finish` from a clean main checkout, or verify the commit in a worktree
   and re-push").
3. Refuse when the tree is dirty (excluding declared expected-dirty paths) even if the
   `HEAD` matches, because no green run there is evidence about the pushed commit.
4. Keep the existing behaviour otherwise: the suite still runs with
   `--scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`, cache mirroring intact,
   feature-branch pushes untouched, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` still bypassing the gate (and the
   guard) explicitly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — capture the gated `local_sha` in the stdin loop (currently
  discarded, `while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha`); add the
  mismatch + dirty checks and their refusal messages inside the
  `need_full_suite = 1` gate block; leave `mirror_suite_cache` and the worklog-sync tail
  alone.
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` — extend `_hook()` with a `local_sha` override (default
  `HEAD`) and a dirty-tree setup; new tests for (a) `local_sha` ≠ `HEAD` refused with
  both SHAs named and `_marker()` empty, (b) dirty tree at matching `local_sha` refused,
  (c) clean matching tree still runs the full suite (existing coverage keeps passing),
  (d) feature-branch push with a mismatched sha still skips the suite.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — new subsection "The gate verifies the pushed commit" with the
  refusal conditions, messages, recovery, and the reproduction recipe (`printf
  '<local-ref> <local-sha> <remote-ref> <zero-sha>
' | sh .githooks/pre-push …` with a
  sha that is not `HEAD`); keep the existing simulate-a-push recipe consistent.
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` — no logic change expected (it only sets
  `core.hooksPath` and repairs the exec bit); confirm it stays a no-op for this change.
- Framework follow-up (out of scope, not edited here):
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (Step 5 ~5141–5216, Step 6 push
  ~5235, finish report) and `~/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push`.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 — "dev-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong tree on the
  non-fast-forward retry path" (open, bug).** Shares the identical invariant and the
  same hook guard (its AC1: "a mismatch between the push cwd's `HEAD` and the pushed
  `local_sha` must never silently verify the wrong tree: gate it correctly or refuse with
  an actionable message"). Per Q2 = B the guard is implemented **once** under whichever
  item is scheduled first; the other becomes verification of its own trigger scenario.
- LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND — discovering item (post-push verification of its dev push
  surfaced the gap).
- LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ — "Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout
  (`core.hooksPath` unset)" — the gate's activation history and the same
  `run_tests.py --summary` = `missing` signal.
- LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK — activated `core.hooksPath` and pinned the context-budget
  thresholds (the gate family this item hardens).
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — the gate's contract, escape hatches and the
  "simulate a `dev` push" recipe.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (framework) — `implement.py finish` pushes from the
  main checkout by design; the reason the framework alternative (Q1 option C) was not
  taken.

## Risks & assumptions

- *Risk: fail-closed blocks a finish whenever the main checkout is dirty or stale.* That
  is the intended release-gate behaviour; the refusal message names the one-step recovery
  (clean the main checkout and re-run `implement.py finish`), and `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` /
  `--no-verify` remain explicit escapes. The main checkout of this repo is clean at
  intake time, so routine finishes are unaffected.
- *Risk: false refusal on legitimate multi-ref pushes.* Mitigation: the guard evaluates
  only `refs/heads/dev|main` targets and ignores deletion (all-zero) shas; tests cover a
  feature-branch ref sharing the same push.
- *Risk: the guard is bypassed by a push that never runs the hook* (`--no-verify`).
  Out of scope — documented escape hatch, not silently allowed.
- *Risk: scope creep into the framework.* The framework half (finish report naming the
  verified tree, pushing from the worktree, propagating the guard to every consumer
  repo's hook copy) stays a linked follow-up, not part of this item.
- *Assumption: the cache fingerprint semantics stay as-is* (`HEAD` + dirty content); the
  guard makes the precondition match the fingerprint rather than redefining the key.
- *Assumption: `implement.py` keeps pushing from the main checkout*, so a skipped
  fast-forward now surfaces as a refused push with an actionable message instead of a
  silent green gate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Evidence gathered before asking (so the questions were not repo-search answerable):
`.githooks/pre-push` discards `local_sha`; `test_cache.compute_git_state()` keys on
`HEAD` + dirty content; `implement.py` Step 5 only *warns* when the fast-forward is
skipped and still pushes from `repo_root`; `tests/test_git_hooks.py::_hook()` always
sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`; the main checkout of this repo is clean.

- **Q1 (shape + scope).** Which fix shape, in which repository?
  - A: repo-local fail-closed guard in `.githooks/pre-push` + regression test; framework
    improvement as a linked follow-up.
  - B: repo-local "gate the pushed commit" via a throwaway detached worktree at
    `local_sha`.
  - C: framework-only change (`implement.py`), requiring agent-infrastructure
    authorisation.
  - **Recommended:** A.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-29): A** — repo-local fail-closed
    guard in `.githooks/pre-push`, with the framework follow-up kept out of scope.
- **Q2 (overlap with LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3).**
  - A: transfer this item's distinct ACs onto that item and close this as duplicate.
  - B: keep both; implement the shared guard once under whichever is scheduled first and
    link the other as verification-only.
  - **Recommended:** B.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-29): B** — both items stay; one
    implementation of the guard, the other item verifies its own trigger.
- **Q3 (strictness when `HEAD` == `local_sha` but the tree is dirty).**
  - A: run the gate anyway with a warning.
  - B: refuse — a dirty fingerprint can never match the pushed commit's clean
    fingerprint, so `run_tests.py --summary` at the pushed commit stays `missing`.
  - **Recommended:** B (excluding project-declared expected-dirty paths; none declared
    here).
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-29): B** — refuse on a dirty tree as
    well as on a HEAD mismatch.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3** – Investigate: dev-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong tree on the non-fast-forward retry path (open)
- **LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ** – Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout (core.hooksPath unset) (completed)
- **LP-0MVT26S4J0021ST3** – Prove the dev-push gate refuses a failing skill test (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+358 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+358 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+358 more)

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator I need a **measured, reproducible verdict** on whether
`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` (the `amd_gpu_metrics_v3_0` blob, the
interface `amdgpu_top` reads) carries a *graded* GFX-activity signal on this
Strix Halo APU — one that separates compute from idle the way the
power-derived `gpu:computing:bool` rule does but `gpu_busy_percent` does not —
and, only if such a field passes an explicit discrimination bar, to have it
published as a Prometheus series through the existing 10 s textfile sampler.
A negative verdict, recorded with numbers so the path is never retried, is an
equally valid outcome.

## Problem statement

The usage report's GPU busy time infers activity from power draw
(`gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`), which cannot tell GFX work from any other
power draw. `gpu_busy_percent` was eliminated as a utilisation signal
(2026-10-28: 45.2 % false-busy, Pearson r = 0.28 against power,
LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL), leaving `gpu_metrics` as the last candidate hardware
activity source. **Intake measurements (2026-10-29) show that candidate is very
probably dead too**: `average_gfx_activity` read **100 % on every one of 120
samples across two captures** while package power moved between 42 W and 123 W
and DRAM bandwidth between 0.7 and 59.5 GB/s. This item therefore exists to
settle the question with evidence and a stated bar, not to assume the answer.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Is the GPU actually doing work right now, and was it
  busy between 17:00 and 19:00?" — needs a utilisation figure that is a direct
  measurement, not a power-draw proxy.
- **Agent answering a usage/incident question (secondary).** Needs to know which
  hardware fields are trustworthy on this host so it cites a real signal instead
  of re-litigating `gpu_busy_percent`.

User stories:

- As an operator I can run one command that decodes `gpu_metrics`, samples it
  alongside power and `gpu_busy_percent`, and prints per-field discrimination
  statistics — so the verdict rests on numbers I can reproduce.
- As an operator I am told plainly whether the interface gives a graded signal,
  with the capture date, kernel, sample counts and band means, so I never
  re-investigate it.
- As an operator, if a field does pass, the series appears next to the existing
  `gpu_*` textfile series without a new daemon, port or scrape job.

## Existing state (measured during intake, 2026-10-29, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic)

| Question | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Is the file live and readable? | `-r--r--r-- 4096` root:root; 264 bytes of content; values change between reads; no root, no ROCm, no `amd-smi` needed |
| Which structure? | Header decodes to `structure_size=264, format_revision=3, content_revision=0` → `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`; the same header text is vendored in `libdrm_amdgpu_sys`'s `wrapper_gpu_metrics.h`) |
| Does the layout check out? | Field sizes under `#pragma pack(4)` sum to 260 B; 4 B tail padding = **264 B**, matching `structure_size` exactly. Cross-checks: `average_socket_power` 95 060 mW vs hwmon `power1_average` 95.06 W (0.1 % agreement); `average_gfx_power` 11.3–44.2 W; `average_gfxclk_frequency` 2 711–2 900 MHz; `average_dram_reads` 0.7–59.5 GB/s; `average_vcn_activity` 0; `average_ipu_activity` all 0; `temperature_gfx` 56–69 °C |
| Does the activity field discriminate? | **No.** Capture A (60 samples @1 s): power 44–123 W, DRAM 1.8–59.5 GB/s → `average_gfx_activity` = 100 on all 60. Capture B (60 samples @1 s): power 42–66 W (idle band), DRAM 0.7–3.5 GB/s → 100 on all 60. Spot samples earlier: 97, 99, 100 at 41–57 W |
| How does it compare with the rejected counter? | Identically saturated: `gpu_busy_percent` = 100 on all 120 samples of both captures; `rocm-smi --showuse` reports `GPU use 100 %` at 54 W. GFX clock is pinned at its 2 900 MHz maximum in *both* bands, so the GFX domain is never gated while the proxy holds the device |
| What *does* vary with load? | `average_dram_reads`/`average_dram_writes` (memory bandwidth, 0.7 → 59.5 GB/s), `average_gfx_power` (11.3 → 44.2 W), `average_socket_power` (42 → 123 W), `average_core_c0_activity` (per-core C0 residency) |
| Are the values instantaneous? | No — they are SMU **time filtered** (`time_filter_alphavalue` = 1 000 000); the filter window is undocumented, so no claim finer than the sample interval is supportable |

Existing pipeline this would plug into: `gpu-metrics.service` runs
`~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` every 10 s, writing `gpu.prom` into
node_exporter's textfile collector (`gpu_busy_percent`, `gpu_vram_*`,
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes`, label `gpu="card0"`), scraped every 15 s by Prometheus;
documented in [docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service](../../docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service)
and [monitoring/README.md](../../monitoring/README.md).

## Desired change

1. **A reproducible probe CLI** — `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py`: decode the
   v3.0 blob from a sysfs path (default
   `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`), sample every candidate activity
   field alongside the two reference signals (amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` and
   `gpu_busy_percent`) at a configurable interval for a configurable duration,
   and emit CSV or `--json`. A `--verdict` mode prints the per-field
   discrimination statistics against the bar below.
2. **A recorded verdict** — the measured numbers plus a pass/fail decision per
   candidate field, written into the work item and the two monitoring documents,
   so the interface is either adopted once or closed off permanently.
3. **Conditional publication** — only if a field passes the bar, publish it
   through the existing 10 s textfile sampler (new `# HELP`/`# TYPE` series with
   the `gpu="card0"` label, atomic write, nothing written on read failure). If
   nothing passes, publish nothing and record why.
4. **A regression guard** — a saturated activity field must not be usable as a
   utilisation input in any rule or report query without a test failing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decodes `gpu_metrics` into named fields
  using the pinned v3.0 layout and validates the header
  (`structure_size` == layout size, `format_revision` == 3); unit tests cover a
  real 264-byte capture committed as a fixture, a truncated buffer, and an
  unknown `format_revision`/`structure_size`, which must be rejected with a
  clear error rather than misparsed.
- [ ] A capture (`--duration`/`--interval`, defaults documented) writes one row
  per sample containing a timestamp, every candidate activity field,
  `power1_average_watts` and `gpu_busy_percent`; a test drives the sampler
  against fixture sysfs trees (fake `/sys/class/drm/card0/device` and hwmon
  directory) and asserts row count, monotonic timestamps and fixture-derived
  values, without sleeping.
- [ ] `--verdict` reports, per candidate field, the idle-band mean (< 60 W), the
  compute-band mean (≥ 90 W), their separation in percentage points, Pearson r
  against package power, and the idle-band false-busy share (samples ≥ 90 %
  while power < 60 W); a field passes only if separation ≥ 30 pp **and**
  r ≥ 0.6 **and** idle-band false-busy ≤ 10 %. Unit tests drive synthetic
  saturated, graded and noisy series and assert the exact pass/fail decision and
  the printed statistics.
- [ ] The measured numbers and the resulting verdict — positive **or** negative
  — are recorded in `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`,
  `monitoring/README.md` (the "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`?"
  section gains a `gpu_metrics` row) and the work item, including capture date,
  kernel version, sample counts and band statistics; a negative verdict is a
  complete outcome, not a failure.
- [ ] If a field passed, the 10 s textfile sampler publishes it (series name,
  `# HELP`/`# TYPE`, `gpu="card0"` label) with the existing atomic-write and
  write-nothing-on-failure behaviour, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`
  documents the series and its meaning; a test runs the sampler against fixture
  sysfs and asserts its emitted series set exactly matches the set the
  documentation table lists (so docs and behaviour cannot drift). If no field
  passed, no new series is added and the test asserts the sampler's series set is
  unchanged.
- [ ] The pinned-counter guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
  (`FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`) is extended so a saturated activity field cannot
  appear as a utilisation input — `gpu_busy_percent` always, and the
  `gpu_metrics` activity fields when the verdict is negative — with a regression
  test that fails if any `monitoring/*.yaml` rule expression or the probe's own
  utilisation expressions select one.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, docstrings, `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` and
  `monitoring/README.md`; the probe's re-measure procedure (how to re-run the
  capture after a kernel, firmware or driver change) is documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- **No new daemon, port or scrape job.** Reuse `gpu-metrics.service` →
  node_exporter textfile collector; the sampler's 10 s cadence and Prometheus's
  15 s scrape interval are the resolution floor and must be stated as such.
- **Host state is part of the deliverable.** The sampler script lives in
  `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` and is documented in
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`; any change to its series must be reflected
  there so a clean clone can reproduce it.
- **Repository boundary.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (`gpu_busy.py`,
  `reporting.py`) is not edited — adopting a passing field in the daily report is
  a follow-up item, mirroring the constraint recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W.
- **The layout must be pinned in-repo.** The struct is not shipped in the
  installed `linux-headers` packages on this host, so the field table must be
  transcribed with a cited source (`struct gpu_metrics_v3_0`) and validated
  against the observed 264-byte `structure_size`; it must fail closed when the
  kernel reports a different revision.
- **No instantaneous claims.** The values are SMU time-filtered with an
  undocumented window; the output must say so rather than imply per-second
  fidelity.
- **Read cost.** One 264-byte sysfs read per sample; world-readable, no root, no
  ROCm userspace, no `amd-smi`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. v3.0 decoder (field table + header
  validation), paired sampler for `gpu_metrics` + hwmon power + `gpu_busy_percent`,
  band statistics and the pass/fail verdict; CSV and `--json` output.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. Decoder fixtures (real 264-byte
  capture, truncated, unknown revision), fixture-sysfs sampling, verdict
  arithmetic and boundary cases (power exactly 60 W / 90 W, activity exactly
  90 %).
- `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` — New. One committed real capture so the
  layout assertion is reproducible.
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` — Record the verdict, the decode layout and
  (conditionally) the new series; extend the verification section with the probe
  command.
- `monitoring/README.md` — Add `gpu_metrics` to "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi`
  or `amdtop`?" with the measured band statistics; note the re-measure recipe.
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` — Header comment records the `gpu_metrics`
  verdict (no rule change expected; the power rule stays authoritative).
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`
  so saturated activity fields are rejected as utilisation inputs.
- `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` — Only if a field passed: emit the new
  series from the same atomic write.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: the premise is false.** Intake evidence already shows
  `average_gfx_activity` saturated at 100 % from 42 W to 123 W. Mitigation: the
  negative verdict is an explicit, accepted outcome (AC4) and the probe records
  which fields *do* discriminate (DRAM bandwidth, GFX power) for a follow-up.
- **Risk: decoder drift after a kernel or firmware upgrade.** Mitigation: header
  validation plus a committed real capture; the probe refuses unknown revisions
  and the docs carry the re-measure procedure.
- **Risk: undocumented APU field semantics.** `average_gfx_activity` may mean
  "GFX domain powered" rather than "GFX busy" on SMU 14. Mitigation: the bar and
  band statistics decide it, and the interpretation limits are documented.
- **Risk: a capture that misses one band.** A verdict computed only from idle
  samples would be meaningless. Mitigation: AC3 requires both bands, and the
  probe reports per-band sample counts so a one-sided capture is visible.
- **Risk: scope creep** into report integration, new daemons or a full GPU
  telemetry redesign. Mitigation: those are explicit constraints/follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption:** amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` remains the reference compute
  signal (idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W) per
  LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; this item does not re-derive the threshold.
- **Assumption:** the discrimination bar (≥ 30 pp separation, r ≥ 0.6, ≤ 10 %
  idle false-busy) is strict enough — it is far stricter than
  `gpu_busy_percent`'s measured 45.2 % false-busy — and is recorded here so the
  producer can tighten or relax it before implementation.
- **Assumption:** both bands occur on this host within a short window (intake saw
  idle at 42–66 W and compute at 90–123 W within ~15 minutes), so a 30-minute
  capture is sufficient; longer captures are supported by the same CLI.
- **Assumption:** priority stays `high` — the verdict decides whether a direct
  hardware utilisation measure is possible at all on this host, which the usage
  report's honesty goal depends on — even though the likely outcome is a short
  negative report rather than a code change.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL** — Evaluate `amd-smi` as the GPU utilisation source
  (completed). Quantified `gpu_busy_percent`'s saturation (45.2 % false-busy,
  r = 0.28) and filed this item as the remaining avenue. Parent context.
- **LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W** — Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation
  history (in review). Owns the *workload* half (per-slot busy/idle, in-flight
  tasks, the `gpu_utilisation.py` CLI). **Partial overlap only**: that item
  attributes power to llama-server slots; this one judges a *hardware* activity
  field. No CLI or slot work is duplicated here — this item produces a probe and
  a verdict, and its publication step (if any) extends the existing sysfs
  sampler.
- **LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT** — Monitoring: deployable, tailnet-exposed Prometheus
  with honest GPU utilisation (completed) and children: LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48
  (power-derived utilisation rules), LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G (docs for the deployed
  stack). The sampler, units and docs this item extends.
- **LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP** — Fix GPU-wedge false positives (completed):
  established that `gpu_busy_percent` is unusable and power is the
  discriminating signal; the proxy's wedge detector was disabled because of it.
- **LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T** — Grafana dashboard GPU VRAM panel queries series no
  exporter publishes (in progress): the precedent for asserting *published*
  series against documentation, which AC5 reuses.
- **LP-0MVNWULLI006ZYXX** — Cross-check report slot-time against llama-server
  eval timings (independent): the other half of validating the report's busy
  figures.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive operator was available for this intake (auto-dispatched by the
herdr downtime worker at 2026-10-29T03:54:28Z), so each question below was
resolved from host and repository evidence; none is blocking. Each carries the
agent's **Recommended** option, which the producer may override.

- **Q1: Given that `average_gfx_activity` already measures as saturated (100 %
  from 42 W to 123 W), is a documented negative verdict an acceptable
  deliverable for this item?**
  **Recommended:** yes — record the numbers, close the path permanently, and file
  follow-ups for the fields that do discriminate.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the item was written to test the hypothesis,
  not to assume it; the file decodes correctly (264 B v3.0, cross-checked
  against hwmon power) yet its activity field does not respond to load, so the
  honest outcome is a negative verdict with evidence. Source: two 60-sample 1 s
  captures (power 44–123 W and 42–66 W, DRAM 0.7–59.5 GB/s, activity 100 on all
  120 samples), `/tmp` probe using the `kgd_pp_interface.h` v3.0 layout.
- **Q2: If a field does pass the bar, should it replace the power-derived
  `gpu:computing:bool` as the report's GPU busy measure, or be published
  alongside it?**
  **Recommended:** publish alongside; keep power-derived authoritative until its
  own calibration item justifies switching.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): `gpu:computing:bool` is referenced by the
  report (`gpu_busy.py`, `reporting.py`), the alert `GpuComputingSustained` and
  `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`; changing its meaning inside an
  investigation item would break three consumers at once. Publishing an additive
  series keeps the comparison visible, and report adoption stays a follow-up
  (same boundary recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W). Source:
  `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`, `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py`.
- **Q3: Where should the probe live, and how should a passing field reach
  Prometheus — extend the deployed bash textfile sampler, or add a Python
  sampler?**
  **Recommended:** a repo `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decoder plus a one-line
  call from the existing bash sampler; no new unit.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the sampler is a documented 10 s bash loop
  writing `gpu.prom` atomically, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` embeds
  the script verbatim; a second sampler would duplicate the unit, the textfile
  directory and the docs. Decoding a 264-byte binary blob in bash is not
  testable, so the field table belongs in Python with fixture tests. Source:
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`, `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL** – Evaluate amd-smi as the GPU utilisation source for the usage report (record the decision) (completed)
- **LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4** – Proxy usage report: hardware power-based GPU busy time (15s sampling) (completed)
- **LP-0MVSPWLLP008AQXZ** – Use the non-GPU (log-derived) local busy time as the decision-facing utilisation figure (open)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, accepted (+480 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, accepted (+480 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, accepted (+479 more)

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the post-flip window measured against the ≥24 h pre-flip
baseline and a keep/rollback verdict recorded, so the sweep is judged by its
own flip criteria instead of by assumption.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers the evaluation half of parent AC1
(trigger, observation window, verdict) and AC3's "run the report and record the
numbers".

## Nature of the task

This is a **scheduled measurement task, not code work**. It starts only after
the sweep child has shipped to `dev`, been released, and the proxy has been
restarted in a quiet window. It is expected to stay open for the 7-day
observation window; it must not be implemented inside a code session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger, window, flip criteria and rollback, verified against the
   deployed state before the flip is announced.
2. Preconditions verified and recorded on this item: the reservation endpoint
   is live, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline exists (report/baseline child), the
   sweep is deployed (config 30 s / depth 2 active after a quiet-window
   restart), and the flip is announced in a comment with the restart
   timestamp.
3. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` is run over the 7-day post-flip
   window (≥1 000 queue events), with numbers recorded: dead wait per hour vs
   baseline, residual wins as a share of queue events, remote dispatch volume
   change, ticket-backed dispatch count, and the lease-active vs `none` loss
   split.
4. A keep/rollback verdict is recorded against the three flip criteria —
   ≥50 % fall in dead wait per hour, residual wins ≥20 % of queue events,
   remote dispatch volume rise <20 % relative. A rollback reverts the two
   values to 60 / 8, restarts the proxy, and records the observed numbers.
5. If the window is incomplete (fewer than 1 000 queue events, a log-coverage
   gap, or no restart yet), the item stays `blocked`/`open` with the shortfall
   and the missing days stated — never a verdict from partial data.

## Key Files

- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (consumed)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (rollback only)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sweep child (30 s / depth 2 deployed) and the report/baseline
  child (baseline + tool).

# Drift guard: resolved full-suite command set must include hidden skill tests

## Goal

An automated test in `tests/` asserts that the resolved full-suite command set
includes a command targeting `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`, so a
future configuration or resolution change cannot silently re-blind the
dev-push gate (parent AC5).

## Context

Parent: **LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X** — repo full-suite gate never runs
`.pi/skills/*/tests` (529 unenforced tests).

**Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (cross-store, SorraAgents): upstream
`run_tests.py` `full_suite_commands()` must emit an extra explicit-path pytest
command for project-local skill test directories. This child lands the guard
that would have caught the original gap; it must not start before the upstream
rule is installed, because the assertion is red until then.

## Minimal implementation

- New `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py`; resolve the runner exactly like
  `.githooks/pre-push`: repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` first,
  then `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
- Import the resolved module with `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and
  call `full_suite_commands(REPO_ROOT)` — no nested suite execution.
- Assert exactly one command whose pytest initial path targets
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`; assert the canonical repo command
  (`pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`) is still present; assert
  `.pi/test-config.json` has no `suiteCommands` key.
- Failure messages name SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB and `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` so a
  future reader knows what regressed and where the rule is documented.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py`
- `.pi/test-config.json`
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Drift guard.** An automated test in `tests/` asserts that the
  resolved full-suite command set includes a command targeting
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`, and it passes in the repo full
  suite (run via the test skill) once SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB's rule is installed.
- **AC2 — Additive, not a replacement.** The same test asserts the canonical
  repo pytest command is still present, so the skill command is proven
  additive.
- **AC3 — No-pin guard.** The test asserts `.pi/test-config.json` carries no
  `suiteCommands` key, with a failure message explaining that a pin would
  silently drop the skill tests and would also disable changed-scope
  selection.
- **AC4 — Resolver parity.** Runner resolution mirrors `.githooks/pre-push`
  (repo-local first, then the global install); the test imports `run_tests.py`
  through that resolved path and only calls `full_suite_commands()` — it never
  executes a nested suite and completes in well under a second.
- **AC5 — Explicit skip.** If neither runner exists the test skips with a
  reason naming the expected install path (documented limitation, D-P3), so a
  skip stays visible in the report rather than silently passing.


## Dependencies

- **Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (cross-store) — the resolution rule this
  test asserts.
- No sibling dependency: this is the test-first item for the parent's
  enforcement work.

## Deliverables

- `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py` (new module, 3–5 tests).

Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC1 (dispatch half), AC3, AC4.

**Goal:** As an agent operator, when a session that has been served locally falls back to a remote provider, I want the compacted history actually dispatched upstream — and when compaction cannot run, I want the untouched history sent with a WARNING that names why.

**Target outcome:** one gated, idempotent, fail-open hook at the remote dispatch point(s), reusing `evaluate_and_apply_compaction` where its semantics fit.

**Minimal implementation**

1. `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: `async def evaluate_boundary_compaction(srv, config, body_json, session_id, provider_cfg, ...) -> dict` — resolves the knob, reads provenance and the estimate, calls `decide_boundary_compaction`, builds the slot-pinned summariser, runs the summarisation in a worker thread (`asyncio.to_thread`, matching `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`), releases the lease immediately, and rewrites `body_json["messages"]` on success (setting `cache_prompt` and `result`-style metadata keys so the existing `X-Compaction-*` bridge headers can mirror them).
2. `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: call the hook immediately before the remote POST in **both** remote dispatch points — the remote-only cycle (`ptr(...)` near ~:10798) and the mixed local+remote cycle (`ptr_remote(...)` near ~:12430) — after the priority/chain resolution and before `_maybe_record_provider_affinity`.
3. Never double-summarise within one request cycle: reuse the `compaction_evaluated`-style per-request flag (a boundary-specific flag if the assembly flag would mask it) and prove it with a test.
4. Fail-open: any exception, timeout, blank/`EmptySummary` return or absent slot leaves the body byte-identical and dispatches remote; log at **WARNING** with a stable token from `boundary_no_slot`, `boundary_slot_unavailable`, `boundary_summarizer_failed`, `boundary_below_guard`, `boundary_disabled`. No remote summariser fallback.
5. Emit a structured boundary compaction event (`boundary_compaction` / `compaction_event`-style) recording session, slot, est_before/est_after, turns summarised, duration_ms and outcome — reuse `log_compaction_event` rather than a new log format where it fits.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - Fires once per request when the gates pass, and the compacted list is the body sent upstream (asserted on the object handed to the remote dispatcher).
  - Summariser failure / timeout / empty / exception → identical outgoing body, remote dispatch still happens, one WARNING with the correct token.
  - Knob disabled → hook returns immediately, no provenance read cost worth logging, no summariser call.
  - Second invocation in the same cycle is a no-op.
- Automated tests: unit tests for fire-once, fail-open per failure mode, token correctness, and no-double-evaluation.

**Constraints**

- No client-protocol change: behaviour stays inside the proxy; response headers may mirror the existing `X-Compaction-*` bridge (LP-0MU44KSMS002DBWA / LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8).
- Do not re-enable or call the assembly-time path; if `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`'s trigger semantics do not fit, call `decide_boundary_compaction` directly and record why.
- Latency is charged before remote TTFT: keep the guard and timeout bounds from the earlier items; do not add unbounded waits.
- Fail-open in every branch — the hook must never raise into the dispatch loop.

**Risky assumptions**

- Both remote dispatch points are reachable through a shared helper without a third call site (e.g. `proxy/ui.py` embedding routes); if a third site dispatches remote chat traffic, it is added to the same helper and noted here.
- The request body is the authoritative history at the boundary (the session store may lag by the current turn); the hook therefore compacts `body_json["messages"]` and stores the compacted history via `session_manager.update_messages` + `mark_compacted`, inheriting the post-compaction delta heal (LP-0MTXEED8E003EDM8).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `evaluate_boundary_compaction` hook beside `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the two remote dispatch call sites (~:10798, ~:12430).
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — reason tokens / event logging reuse.
- `proxy/proxy/session_manager.py` — compacted-history update + anchors.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — hook tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a request for a session with at least one prior locally-served turn recorded in the session store is about to be dispatched to a `type: remote` provider, the proxy evaluates boundary compaction before the remote request is sent and dispatches the compacted message list upstream when compaction succeeds.
2. Summariser failure, timeout, empty/blank summary, absence of an assigned slot or an exception leaves the outgoing history byte-identical to today and still dispatches remote — an empty summary is never injected and turns are never silently dropped (existing `EmptySummary` / `remote_with_guidance` guarantees preserved).
3. No remote summariser fallback: every skip is logged at WARNING with a stable machine-readable reason token (`boundary_no_slot`, `boundary_slot_unavailable`, `boundary_summarizer_failed`, `boundary_below_guard`) and the request proceeds remote untouched.
4. A structured compaction-event log line records session, slot, est_before/est_after, turns summarised, duration and outcome for every boundary evaluation.
5. Boundary evaluation is idempotent per request cycle (exactly one summarisation, no re-evaluation), and unit tests cover fire-once plus each fail-open failure mode.
data.title: Boundary compaction hook on remote dispatch (fail-open)

Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC6 (integration half) and the default-off regression half of AC5.

**Goal:** As a proxy maintainer, I want an integration test that drives the real failure-to-remote path — session served locally, then escalated — so the trigger, the summariser call count, the compacted body on the wire and the slot release ordering are proven end-to-end rather than only in unit isolation.

**Target outcome:** one integration test module (or a clearly separated section of `test_compaction_boundary_remote.py`) that exercises the dispatch cycles with stubbed HTTP transports, plus the default-off regression test.

**Minimal implementation**

1. Build a harness that (a) creates a session, (b) runs a local completion through the mixed cycle so the session records local provenance, (c) makes the next request bypass local (size or explicit remote-only chain) so it routes remote, with `httpx` transport stubs for the local summariser POST and the remote POST.
2. Assert exactly one summarisation call, that its body carries the assigned `id_slot`, and that the remote POST body carries the summary marker plus the retained system prompt and first user message verbatim.
3. Assert ordering: release of the local lease is recorded before the remote stream starts, and the lease registry holds no entry afterwards.
4. Regression: with `server.remote_boundary_compaction: false`, assert zero summariser calls and a dispatch body identical to the pre-change behaviour.
5. Cover the two unchanged cases: a session with no prior local service, and a session below the minimum-size guard.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - Exactly one summarisation call per boundary evaluation (no double evaluation in a cycle).
  - Remote request body contains the summary marker and the verbatim retention set.
  - Release precedes remote stream start; no leaked lease.
  - Knob disabled → identical dispatch body, no summariser call (byte-comparison against the un-compacted body).
- Automated tests: the integration module is green via the test skill; no live backend, GPU or network.

**Constraints**

- Use the repo's existing stubbing patterns for `httpx` and the provider/remote cycles; do not add a live-endpoint test.
- Do not weaken or delete existing compaction tests; this item adds coverage only.
- Keep runtime under a few seconds — no sleeps, no retry waits.

**Risky assumptions**

- The mixed cycle can be made to bypass local deterministically (size threshold or a remote-only chain) without depending on GPU state; if not, the remote-only cycle is used and the local provenance seeded through the session manager plus a prior local-dispatch unit path.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — integration + regression tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_bypass_wiring.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_integration.py` — harness patterns to reuse.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the cycles under test.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — the hook under test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An integration test drives a session that is served locally and then routed remote, asserting exactly one summarisation call for the boundary compaction.
2. The integration test asserts the compacted body (summary marker plus the verbatim retention set) is what reaches the remote provider on the wire.
3. The integration test asserts the session's local dispatch lease is released and, with an ordering assertion, that the release precedes the remote stream start.
4. The boundary compaction is controlled by its own independent knob `server.remote_boundary_compaction` (default `false`) that does not re-enable assembly-time compaction, ships disabled by default in `proxy/config.yaml`, and leaves request handling unchanged when disabled — the regression test asserts no summariser call and an identical dispatch body.
5. A session with no prior local service, and a session below the agreed minimum-size guard, are asserted to dispatch unchanged.

Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC7.

**Goal:** As a proxy maintainer (and as the operator who must be able to switch this on safely), I want the local→remote boundary compaction documented — its trigger, its own knob, its release ordering and its fail-open behaviour — so enabling it needs no code reading and its relationship to the disabled assembly-time compaction is unambiguous.

**Target outcome:** the operator-facing and developer-facing docs describe the boundary trigger and exactly how to enable, tune and disable it.

**Minimal implementation**

1. `docs/llama-router.md` — a "Boundary compaction (local → remote)" subsection under the session-compaction section: when it fires (remote provider + recorded local provenance + size guard), the slot it uses, the immediate release, the fail-open WARNING tokens, the latency cost and the `X-Compaction-*` mirroring.
2. `proxy/config.yaml` — `remote_boundary_compaction: false` and `remote_boundary_compaction_min_tokens` with explanatory comments stating explicitly that these do **not** re-enable `compaction_trigger_ratio` (which stays `0` per the operator's 2026-09-17 decision, LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6).
3. Module docstrings: `compaction.decide_boundary_compaction`, the slot-pinned summariser builder, and `router_helpers.evaluate_boundary_compaction` — trigger, tokens, KV caveat, why there is no remote summariser fallback.
4. A short "what changed vs LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6" note so a future reader does not mistake this for a re-enable of assembly-time compaction.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - A reader can enable the feature from `docs/llama-router.md` alone (knob name, default, guard, expected log lines).
  - The doc names all four WARNING reason tokens and what each means operationally.
  - `proxy/config.yaml` comments state the independence from `compaction_trigger_ratio` and link the disable decision.
  - Docstrings match the implemented behaviour (verified while writing them).
- Automated tests: no new tests; the docs-only change must not alter behaviour (existing doc-lint / config-load tests stay green).

**Constraints**

- UK English; match the existing documentation tone and heading levels.
- Do not restate or edit the assembly-time compaction design docs beyond a cross-reference.
- No behaviour change in this item.

**Risky assumptions**

- None material: the documentation follows the implemented behaviour from the preceding items. If the implementation deviates from the plan (e.g. one call site instead of two), the doc describes what was built and notes the deviation.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/llama-router.md` — boundary-compaction section.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — knob + guard comments.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py`, `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — module docstrings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/llama-router.md` (compaction section) documents the boundary trigger, its knob and the immediate slot release along with its fail-open behaviour.
2. The new config keys are documented with explanatory comments in `proxy/config.yaml`, shipping disabled by default and stating that they do not re-enable assembly-time compaction.
3. Module docstrings describe the boundary trigger, its fail-open WARNING reason tokens and the slot-reuse KV caveat.
4. An operator can enable, tune and revert the feature from the documentation alone, and the relationship to `LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6` (assembly-time compaction disabled) is stated explicitly.

# Investigate what happens if I switch to a single slot

## Problem statement

The operator is considering serving the local model from a single llama-server
slot (`session_slot_pool_size: 1`, i.e. 1 x 262,144 tokens instead of 2 x
131,072) and needs to know two things before deciding: which routing and
balancing metrics adjust themselves and which stay put, and what a single slot
would do to throughput. Today the answer is spread across `provider.py`
derivation helpers, static config constants, log-consuming analysis scripts and
one heavily-gated measurement experiment, so there is no single, auditable
answer.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** deciding the local slot geometry.
  *"As the operator, I want to know exactly which mechanisms follow a 2 -> 1
  slot change by themselves and which I must change by hand, so I do not
  switch geometry and silently get the old routing behaviour."*
- **Work-item pipeline owner** judging whether single-slot serving would slow
  the herdr work-item cadence.
  *"As the pipeline owner, I want a reasoned, quantified prediction of turns
  and tokens served locally over time, so I can tell whether fewer slots cost
  throughput or only latency."*
- **Agent maintainer / on-call** relying on metrics to spot a single-slot
  regression.
  *"As on-call, I want the audit to tell me which existing metric would reveal
  single-slot starvation, and which ones would stay silent, so I know where the
  blind spots are."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A single-slot impact report exists at `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md`
  with a complete inventory table of every routing/balancing mechanism and
  metric on the local dispatch path. Each row records: its current value at 2
  slots, its computed value at 1 slot, its classification
  (`derived-auto` / `static-needs-manual-change` / `not-applicable`), and
  `file:line` evidence. The inventory must cover at least: per-slot context,
  physical per-slot clamp, economic warm ceiling, absolute warm cap, cold
  threshold, hard-routing cap, `session_slot_tenants`, the dispatch lease pool
  (`max_local`), `local_max_concurrent_prefills`, contention-queue
  wait/depth/lease-grace/ETA-ordering, slot-exhaustion retries, `/health` and
  `/llama/local/status` counts plus per-slot detail, the usage-analysis report
  metrics (local busy %, turns served locally, input/output tokens processed
  locally, diverts by reason, queue waits, dispatch-to-first-byte, prefill and
  decode slot-seconds, decode tok/s), the Prometheus `llama_slots_*` counters,
  and herdr's consumption of the status endpoint.
- AC2: The report states the headline answer explicitly: how many inventory
  items auto-adjust, which items stay static, and the exact
  `key: old -> new` list required for a coherent single-slot switch. It must
  state that the configured absolute warm cap (120,000) and economic-ceiling
  ratio (0.4578) keep the effective warm ceiling at 120,000 even though the
  physical per-slot clamp doubles to 258,048, so doubling the per-slot context
  routes nothing extra on its own. The one-line verdict is also recorded as a
  comment on this work item.
- AC3: A reasoned throughput-impact analysis at request level, **including
  tokens processed locally**, with a named mechanism and a sourced baseline for
  every conclusion: turns served locally and tokens processed locally
  (prompt/completion), per-session first-byte and decode latency,
  head-of-line blocking and queue waits, slot reuse/thrash and re-prefill
  volume, and concurrency headroom. Each conclusion identifies the metric and
  the A/B arm comparison that would confirm or refute it. Token figures must
  state their provenance: the report's `Stream finished`
  `tokens=prompt/completion/total` lines (authoritative) versus any derived
  estimate, and how local versus remote turns are split.
- AC4: A metrics-gap list: for each single-slot conclusion, state whether an
  existing metric can detect it. Every blind spot is filed as a follow-up work
  item (e.g. the blocked slot-occupancy metrics LP-0MVT1O0VG00905EL) rather
  than implemented in this item.
- AC5 (testing/validation): New or extended unit tests pin the derivations the
  audit relies on — at 1 and at 2 slots, the physical clamp, effective warm
  ceiling (including the absolute-cap dominance), cold threshold and
  hard-routing cap resolve to the values the report documents — so the report's
  claims are executable and future config drift fails the suite.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular,
  cross-links and any comment that asserts a fixed 2-slot pool are corrected in
  `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`,
  `proxy/config.yaml`, `models.ini` and `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/
  REFERENCE.md`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Desk analysis only** (producer answer 1A). No live geometry flip, no
  proxy/llama-server restart and no arm measurement: the measured comparison
  belongs to LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN, whose arms are gated on a >= 60 % busy night.
- Read-only runtime inspection is limited to the existing `/health` and
  `/llama/local/status` endpoints and must not add GPU load or contend for a
  slot.
- Every claim cites `file:line` or a measured baseline with its window and
  source. No unsourced numbers.
- No new metrics and no configuration-value changes in this item (producer
  answer 3B): gaps become follow-up items, behaviour changes become separate
  items. Factually wrong comments may be corrected.
- The report is a prediction plus an auto-adjustment audit. It must not be
  written as, or pre-empt, the A/B verdict.

## Existing state (seed evidence to verify and extend)

- Current base geometry: `session_slot_pool_size: 2`,
  `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, warm cap 120,000, cold 38,000, economic
  ratio 0.4578 (`proxy/config.yaml:1685`, `:1332`, `:1297`, `:1410`). The
  per-mode overlays are retired, so `config.yaml` is authoritative
  (`proxy/proxy/config_merge.py`).
- Per-slot context is derived, never configured:
  `effective_per_slot_threshold(ctx, slots) = ctx // slots - 4096`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:1816`), i.e. 126,976 at 2 slots and 258,048 at 1.
- WARM resolves through the 3-term model
  (`provider.py:1930`-`2010`): economic ceiling
  `round(ratio x ctx)` capped by the absolute warm config, then clamped by the
  physical per-slot threshold and the hard-routing cap. With today's constants
  `min(round(0.4578 x 262144) = 120,010, 120,000) = 120,000`, so warm stays
  120,000 at one slot.
- COLD is an economic new-token threshold and is explicitly **not** scaled or
  clamped (`provider.py:1955`-`1968`); the `(cold, warm]` band must not collapse
  (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- Queue and prefill knobs are static, not slot-derived:
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60`, `contention_queue_max_depth: 8`,
  `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300`, ETA ordering on
  (`proxy/config.yaml:1756`-`1788`), and `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`
  (`:1706`), so prefill is already serialised with two slots and a second slot
  only overlaps decode.
- Auto-adjusting items already identified: `session_slot_tenants` defaults to
  the resolved slot count ("N tenants, N slots", `config.yaml:1378`); the
  dispatch lease pool `max_local` reads `session_slot_pool_size`
  (`provider.py:6172`); runtime counts and per-slot detail come from
  llama-server `/slots` / `/props` (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`) and are
  consumed by `/health`, `/llama/local/status` and herdr's per-slot dispatch
  (LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ, cross-repo WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F).
- Per-slot occupancy metrics are **not** published yet
  (LP-0MVT1O0VG00905EL, blocked) — a likely gap for detecting single-slot
  starvation.
- The single-slot (Arm B) threshold values are already defined:
  warm 258,048, economic ratio 0.9844, cold 38,000
  (`docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` section 3.1).
- Baselines available for the throughput reasoning: a 24 h window with 2,064
  `context_too_large` diverts, 105 of them from already-warm sessions at
  126-137K tokens; local idle 89.8 % serving 225 turns over 26 sessions;
  measured concurrency average 1.04 while busy with peak 2; prefill dominating
  local response time (prompt-eval p50 16 s, p90 189 s, max 591 s); 43.8 M
  tokens/day re-prefilled (`docs/dev/slot-reuse-gap-final-report.md` section 3).
- Known counter-evidence for fewer slots: inter-session slot thrash invalidates
  cached prefixes (`docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`, "cache preservation:
  poor") and 27 sessions were observed cycling through 2 slots in 5.4 h
  (`proxy/config.yaml` comment at `:1371`).

## Desired change

A decision-grade, evidence-cited analysis of single-slot serving: (a) the
derived-vs-static inventory and the exact coupled config changes a coherent
switch needs, (b) a request-level throughput prediction including tokens
processed locally, with the confirming metric named for each claim, (c) a
metrics-gap list with filed follow-ups, and (d) unit tests pinning the
derivations, plus documentation cross-links. No runtime behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` — the new report (main deliverable)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `effective_per_slot_threshold`,
  `_effective_large_context_thresholds`, `effective_large_context_economic_ceiling`,
  `compute_hard_routing_cap`, `_get_active_local_slots`, dispatch lease pool
- `proxy/config.yaml` — slot/ctx/threshold/queue keys and their comments
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `/slots` counts, per-slot detail,
  `/llama/local/status` payload
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — status endpoint consumers
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `aggregation.py`, `reporting.py`, `REFERENCE.md` — request/token/divert/queue
  metric sources
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_per_slot_ctx.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_hard_routing_cap.py`, `tests/test_ctx_slot_validation.py` —
  existing threshold tests to extend
- `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` —
  protocol/design docs to cross-link
- `models.ini` — launch-flag comments describing per-slot context

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (scope substitution):** the report could be read as the geometry
  decision. Mitigation: AC2/AC3 language makes it a prediction plus audit, and
  the A/B keeps the verdict.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the audit will surface missing metrics and possible
  config defects. Mitigation: follow-up items only (AC4), no implementation.
- **Risk (stale baselines):** concurrency, divert and prefill figures come from
  different windows. Mitigation: every baseline carries its window and source.
- **Risk (uncontended evidence):** current local idle (~90 %) means the
  serialisation cost of one slot is under-observed today; the report must say
  so rather than extrapolate a cheap conclusion.
- **Risk (mis-attributed tokens):** "tokens processed locally" can be computed
  only from `Stream finished` lines carrying provider plus token counts; a
  fallback or a missing usage line can silently shift the split. Mitigation:
  state the attribution rule and the count of lines without token evidence.
- **Assumption:** "single slot" means `session_slot_pool_size: 1` with
  unchanged `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, i.e. 1 x 262,144 per-slot context
  and clamp 258,048 (Arm B geometry), not a reduced total context.
- **Assumption:** producer answers fix the scope as desk analysis (1A),
  request-level throughput including tokens processed locally (2A), and
  existing metrics plus a gaps list (3B).

## Related work

- **LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN** (Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K
  ctx) — partial overlap: it owns the measured A/B and is gated on a >= 60 %
  busy night. This item delivers only the auto-adjustment audit and the
  reasoned prediction, and must not duplicate its measurement ACs.
- **LP-0MVT1O0VG00905EL** (blocked: Publish slot occupancy metrics from the
  proxy) — likely the main metric gap for a single-slot regime.
- **LP-0MVHT41X9000AXFB** (open: Stale warm-threshold constants in
  eval/analysis scripts) — same family of static-constant drift.
- **LP-0MTZUZR7K009Q98J** (open: drop `slot_schedule` dependency after
  per-mode slot-count simplification) — analysis tooling that may still assume
  slot geometry.
- **LP-0MU03AL730000B5W** (per-mode slot counts 1/1/3) — superseded by the
  single-config change LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA; its numbers must not be quoted as
  current.
- Threshold lineage: **LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1** (per-slot clamp),
  **LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN** (3-term warm model),
  **LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP** (band collapse),
  **LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95** (warm cap vs economic ceiling).
- Queue behaviour under one slot: **LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6** (ETA ordering),
  **LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP** (lease-owner retention),
  **LP-0MTH7JX82000YS5N** (generating-only occupancy).
- Docs: `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`,
  `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md`,
  `docs/dev/contention-queue-queue-caps-vs-slots.md`,
  `docs/dev/slot-reuse-gap-final-report.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (2026-10-29)

- Q1 "Deliverable scope — (a) desk analysis only (audit derived vs hardcoded +
  reasoned throughput prediction, measurement left to the blocked A/B),
  (b) desk analysis plus flip live config now, (c) full measurement now?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-10-29): **(a) desk analysis
  only**. Source: producer reply; recorded on the work item as a comment.
  Research: the measurement already exists as LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN (open,
  `plan_complete`, arms blocked on the > 60 % busy gate; protocol in
  `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md`).
- Q2 "What should 'throughput of work items' be measured as — (a) request/turn
  level translated to herdr cadence, (b) wl work items only, (c) both?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-10-29): **(a) request/turn level,
  and include tokens processed locally**. Source: producer reply. Research: the
  usage-analysis report already emits turns, `Total tokens`
  (input/output/total with fast/cheap and by-model splits) and per-session
  decode tok/s (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`), so no new
  metric is needed for this.
- Q3 "Metric inventory scope — (a) only metrics that exist today, (b) existing
  metrics plus a gaps list with follow-up items?" — Answer (producer,
  interactive reply 2026-10-29): **(b) existing plus gaps list**. Source:
  producer reply. Research: per-slot occupancy metrics are not published yet
  (LP-0MVT1O0VG00905EL, blocked), which is precisely the blind spot a gaps list
  must capture; follow-ups are filed rather than implemented.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MTZUZR7K009Q98J** – proxy-usage-analysis: drop slot_schedule dependency after per-mode slot-count simplification (open)
- **LP-0MRO4U5O1008TLFU** – Write multi-slot tests for poll_slots_for_model() (completed)
- **LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L** – Fix poll_slots_for_model() to iterate all slots (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+402 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+402 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+402 more)
