## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard (or the queue
admit criterion) to price the blocker class the diagnosis proves is holding the
slot — so a queue wait that cannot be served inside the 60 s budget is refused
up-front instead of burning the full budget and detouring remote — or, if the
diagnosis does not support a change, a committed decision that says so.

This is the behaviour-change slice. It is deliberately gated on the diagnosis
record so the change is driven by evidence, not by the assumption that the
guard is "too permissive".

## Context (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Measured in the post-change 24 h window: 314/517 enqueued waits abandoned, all
at the full budget; 225/314 were `reason=local_lease_active`; for the 176
abandonments with a session-level preceding guard decision, 170 were `admit`
with median `projected_wait_s = 35.8 s`. The guard's occupancy term prices peer
*prefill* service (including the re-priced occupant remaining new tokens from
`LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ`) but not the *generation* time of a lease holder that
keeps the slot after its prefill.

## Scope

- Extend the projected-wait quantity so the diagnosed blocker class is priced
  (for example, a lease/decode hold term raised into the existing occupancy
  maximum — evidence can only raise the floor, never lower it), and/or refuse
  a queue admit whose remaining budget cannot outlast the blocker.
- Preserve every documented invariant: measured evidence can only raise the
  symmetric `eta * busy_slots` floor; fail-open on missing/invalid records;
  warm prompts unchanged; no new configuration knob; `high` priority never
  queues.
- Out of scope: capping the lease holder's consecutive renewals — that is
  `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0`.

## Minimal implementation

- Test first: simulated blockers in `proxy/tests/` — (a) a blocker whose
  remaining generation/lease hold exceeds the remaining budget ⇒ refuse (or
  defer under the pin semantics), (b) a short-prefill blocker ⇒ admit exactly
  as today, (c) missing/invalid occupant record ⇒ fail-open (today's floor).
- Then the minimal guard change in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (plus the
  caller plumbing in `provider.py`/`router_helpers.py` if the blocker snapshot
  is not already available) and the log fields that make the new term
  attributable.
- Document the rollback using existing knobs only
  (`local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off`,
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A unit test shows a blocker whose remaining generation/lease hold exceeds the remaining queue budget causes a refusal (or the pin-semantics deferral) instead of a full-budget queue wait; a short-prefill blocker still admits with the same decision as today.
- AC2: The change only prices the blocker class named by the diagnosis, never lowers the symmetric `eta * busy_slots` floor, and a test asserts fail-open on missing/invalid occupant evidence (no guessed multiplier).
- AC3: Guardrails untouched and asserted: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60), `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120), ordering `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` green, no new configuration knob, `high` priority never queues.
- AC4: Rollback is documented using existing knobs only, in `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md`, and the page names this item and the diagnosis record as the evidence.
- AC5: The new decision term appears in the `local_admission_guard` log line (parsed by the usage report) so the post-fix window can attribute refusals to it.
- AC6: If the diagnosis does not justify a behaviour change, this item closes with a committed decision note instead of code, recording the measured rationale and re-scoping AC1-AC3 in a comment (no silent no-op).
- AC7: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; existing prefill-ETA, deadline, occupancy and budget tests pass unchanged in intent.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_occupancy_deadline_admission.py`, `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_contended.py`, `proxy/tests/test_occupant_remaining_rebase.py`
- `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md`

## Related

- Parent: `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR`; blocked-by: abandoned-wait diagnosis, lease-active re-queue path fixes.
- `LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ` — occupant-remaining re-pricing (the term being extended).
- `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0` — lease fairness (out of scope, linked evidence).

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want a 24 h post-fix measurement of the
abandoned-queue-wait share, compared against the diurnally matched baseline and
the literal 85 % bar, so the regression item can be closed on evidence — or
kept open with numbers that say the fix did not work.

## Scheduling (learned from LP-0MVTKTOVI006ZONN)

- **Runnable at/after** (fix deploy timestamp + 24 h); the window end is fixed
  by the deploy of the behaviour-change sibling, not by "the last 24 h".
- **Do not run early.** A session starting before the window has elapsed stands
  down (claim nothing, edit nothing) and says so — a sub-24 h slice is not the
  record, and the 13 h slice taken on 2026-10-29 already showed a slice is not
  a substitute.
- Log retention: proxy logs rotate ~6 h with gzip retention back to
  `2026-10-15`; run within ~3 days of the window end.

## Scope

- Measure the fixed 24 h window with the fixed harness (own-request banding,
  trigger/cause split, contiguous-wait accounting) and the usage report.
- Compare against three references: literal 85 % bar; diurnally matched
  pre-change baseline (52.6 %); pre-fix post-change share (60.7 %).
- Count and explain `local_eviction_after_acceptance` by reason (no new class ⇒
  link a triage item if one appears).
- Update the operator docs and both records.

## Minimal implementation

- Commit `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postfix.md` + `.json` produced
  by the committed commands (no hand-typed numbers; the embedded command line
  regenerates the JSON).
- Update `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md` and
  `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md` cross-references.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The fixed 24 h window ending 24 h after the behaviour-change deploy is measured with the fixed harness and committed as `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postfix.{md,json}`, labelled with the deploy commit and both window bounds.
- AC2: The record reports the abandoned share against all three references (literal 85 % bar, diurnally matched pre-change 52.6 %, pre-fix post-change 60.7 %), split by trigger, cause and band, with per-hour rates alongside shares.
- AC3: `local_eviction_after_acceptance` is counted by reason and compared with the previous windows; every class is zero or explained in one line, and any genuinely new class links to a triage work item.
- AC4: Every number is pasted from tool output and the embedded command regenerates the committed JSON byte-for-byte (modulo the rotation-dependent log-file inventory).
- AC5: A session that starts before the window has elapsed stands down without claiming or editing anything (asserted by the record's "window not yet elapsed" note when applicable), mirroring the LP-0MVTKTOVI006ZONN scheduling-hold pattern.
- AC6: `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md` and `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md` are updated, and the closing verdict is recorded on parent `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR` (share met or not, with numbers).

data.description:
# Goal

Bring `slots_stale` under **5 %** of `/llama/local/status` polls (the measured target of
LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 AC1) by making the `/slots` counts/detail refresh meet its handler budgets
under real load — or, if that is not achievable at the configured budgets, establish the evidence
and move the contract deliberately.

# Problem statement

The 24 h re-measurement of 2026-10-29 (window `2026-10-29 01:00 → 2026-10-30 01:00` local,
coverage `covered`, no gaps, 2 proxy restarts inside the window at 12:58:34 and 14:09:25) measured:

| Metric | 24 h value | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Status polls | 26,019 | — |
| `slots_stale=true` | **7,698 (29.59 %)** | < 5 % → **missed** |
| stale source | `detail_cache` 7,224 / `counts_cache` 474 / unknown 0 | — |
| stale-poll refresh latency | ≥5 s 2,063 · 2–5 s 3,888 · 1–2 s 1,637 · <1 s 110 | — |
| `capacity_hint` idle/prefill_bound/saturated/abandoned_busy | 16,160 / 6,156 / 3,293 / 410 | — |
| `saturated` with no live local work | 70 (0.27 % of polls) — 65 attributed, 5 unattributable | 0 |
| herdr downtime dispatches (durable trail) | 81 (target ≥ 10) | **met** |
| Local dispatches | 829 (143 sessions, 29 herdr; warm 576 / cold 253) | — |

Same-window trend of the metric on successive builds:

| Window | Build | `slots_stale` |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-24 20:00 → 07:00 (night) | `56a3a28a`/`2d2b6b51` (router `/slots` path) | 79.61 % |
| 2026-10-28 09:30 → 21:30 (12 h) | child-port resolver `f58e8964` live | 53.92 % |
| 2026-10-29 01:00 → 2026-10-30 01:00 (24 h) | `f58e8964` live + later HEAD | **29.59 %** |

The child-port resolver removed the router from the polling path and roughly halved the stale rate,
but **77 % of the residual stale polls were served from cache after a refresh that took longer than
the 2 s counts / 1.0 s (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`) detail budget**. Staleness is therefore no longer a
router artefact: the `/slots` read path still exceeds its budget under load, so `slots_stale` is
reporting real latency, not a truthfulness defect (the cache-time reconciliation of
LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM still holds — only 70 polls, 0.27 %, showed `saturated` without live work).

# Evidence and re-derivation

- Artifacts: `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_24h-remeasure/` (`measurement.json`,
  `measurement.txt`, `saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`, `prefill_thrash_skips.csv`,
  `SUMMARY.md`, `provenance.json`).
- Command (read-only, verified tool LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK):

  ```bash
  python3 scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py \
    --since '2026-10-29 01:00' --until '2026-10-30 01:00' --window-closed \
    --label 24h-remeasure --limit 250 --json \
    --write-artifacts ~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_24h-remeasure
  ```

- Durable herdr dispatch trail re-derived from `wl export` (`author=herdr-downtime` +
  `Auto-dispatched` + `createdAt` inside the window): 81 dispatches, 53 distinct items.

# Not in scope (tracked elsewhere)

- Router `/slots` HTTP 400 responses — LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 (this item is about latency/staleness,
  not 400s).
- Nightly report generator publishing `slots_stale` / `capacity_hint` — LP-0MVRMHY0F007RWA0.
- Abandoned-dispatch ghosts inflating `abandoned_busy` — LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB.

# Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The `/slots` counts/detail read path is profiled under load and the dominant contributor to
  > 2 s refreshes is named with per-path timing evidence (child-port request concurrency, per-poll
  fan-out, llama-server `/slots` cost, or proxy-side serialisation).
- AC2: A 24 h window re-measured with the same tool shows `slots_stale < 5 %` of status polls;
  **or** the item records that the configured budgets cannot be met at peak load, with the measured
  latency distribution, and the producer decides whether to raise the budget or change the target.
- AC3: `capacity_hint=saturated` without live local work stays at 0, or every residual poll is
  attributed (the 24 h run left 5 unattributable out of 26,019).
- AC4: `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` reflects the outcome, and the full suite is green.

## Related work

- discovered-from:LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 (24 h re-measurement that measured this residual)
- Measurement items: LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ, LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ, LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV
- Fix that this residual survives: LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (capacity truthfulness, unchanged)

# Plan (plan_complete, 2026-10-31)

Decomposition into three vertical phases, test-first. Effort/risk pre-check returned
`decision=plan` (Medium effort, Medium risk); the plan-approval gate returned
`request_approval=false`, so no approval pause was required.

## Evidence refresh (seed for this plan)

Live window 2026-10-31 00:42 → 04:52 local (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`, current HEAD),
read-only analysis:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Status polls | 4,164 |
| `slots_stale=true` | 709 (17.03 %) |
| stale by poll latency | `< 1 s` 11 · `1–2 s` 172 · `2–5 s` 355 · `≥ 5 s` 181 |
| `slot_counts_stale=true` | 0 |
| `slots_detail_stale=true` | 657 |

So the residual is now **entirely the per-slot detail query**, and it is a real latency signal: the
handler awaits `query_llama_status()` (1 s budget) then counts (2 s) then detail
(`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`, 1 s) **in series**, and the detail fetch duplicates work the 1 s periodic
refresher already does (`_last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at`). Idle child-port
`/slots` costs 0.7–5.5 ms, so the cost is load-dependent backend latency, not route cost.

## Phases and children

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Test: /slots read-path freshness contract (LP-0MVVXGHHB0073W1B) | task | — |
| F1 | Instrument per-phase /slots read-path timings (LP-0MVVXGHT1001I5YX) | task | T1 |
| F2 | Profile 24 h window; name dominant contributor (LP-0MVVXGI490089OX5) | task | F1 |
| F3 | Serve shared /slots snapshot on status path (LP-0MVVXGLTM008ROJ9) | feature | T1, F2 |
| F4 | slots_stale from snapshot age; schema 5 (LP-0MVVXGM54009TOXD) | feature | F3 |
| F5 | Attribute saturated-without-live-work residual polls (LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR) | task | F3 |
| F6 | Re-measure 24 h window; record AC2 disposition (LP-0MVVXGMRN007NCJP) | task | F3, F4, F5 |
| F7 | Docs and full-suite green (LP-0MVVXGN2C004O28B) | docs | F6 |

### Phase A — evidence (T1 → F1 → F2)

Tracer bullet through code → `status_request` log → analysis tool → recorded evidence. Ends with the
dominant contributor named per parent AC1, and an explicit instruction that F3/F4 descriptions are
updated if the evidence contradicts the assumed fix.

### Phase B — fix (T1 → F3 → F4/F5)

Tracer bullet through the handler read path → payload/log → consumer contract → attribution. One
shared `/slots` snapshot; counts and detail derived from the same payload; `slots_stale` defined by
snapshot age rather than cache use; stale reconciliation preserved.

### Phase C — verdict (F6 → F7)

Re-measure a full ≥ 24 h window with the same tool and record either `slots_stale < 5 %` (AC2 first
branch) or the measured latency distribution and the producer decision request (AC2 second branch);
then documentation and full suite (AC4).

## Reused implementations (no new machinery where one exists)

- `_fetch_slots_payload()` — TTL caching + single-flight coalescing (LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT).
- `_last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at` — stamped shared snapshot.
- `_resolve_slot_details_for_enrichment()` — pristine-cache discipline (LP-0MVECWYWK000U3E1).
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — `slots_stale_attribution.by_source` /
  `by_latency_band`, `--write-artifacts` (LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK).
- `downgrade_stale_capacity_hint()` — cache-time reconciliation (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM) stays the
  guard that makes snapshot-serving safe.

## Assumptions (documented, not invented requirements)

1. The measured residual is dominated by backend `/slots` latency under load plus per-poll fan-out;
   F2 is the gate that confirms or refutes this before F3 is implemented.
2. A snapshot age of ≤ 2 s (two refresher cycles) is an acceptable freshness budget for a
   dispatcher that polls at ~17 polls/min; the value is env-configurable and revisited in F6.
3. `slots_stale` redefined as age-over-budget is the honest observable; the alternative (keep
   "served from cache") makes the metric unmeasurable once the poll path serves a warm snapshot by
   design. Recorded as OPEN QUESTION Q1 in the Appendix, to be confirmed before F4.
4. The item is a `bug` with four ACs, so no epic-level feature splitting below the eight children.

## Duplicate-work check

`wl search slots_stale` / `/slots latency` / `single-flight slots` / `STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`: no
completed item covers this scope. Nearest relatives and why they are not duplicates:
LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 (measurement, closed with a documented miss), LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ (detail-cache
fallback, delivered), LP-0MVJML600003CQ6Y (single-flight cancellation, delivered),
LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM (post-cancel release lag, different defect), LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (abandoned-work
annotation, delivered).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-31 — initial decomposition: 8 children created (T1, F1–F7), 10 dependency edges wired,
  evidence refresh recorded, AC-section boundary fixed (`# Related work` → `## Related work` so the
  coverage review stops parsing provenance links as acceptance criteria). Stage → `plan_complete`.

# Chat-model child-port fallback fires for unloaded local models (gpt120) — polls the router and pollutes the fallback signal

**Priority:** medium · **Type:** bug · **Stage:** intake paused — scope questions pending producer answers (see Appendix)

## Problem statement

When a chat request names a local model that is **not currently loaded** (e.g.
`gpt120` while `Qwen3` is resident), the proxy's slot-availability check still
tries to discover that model's child port, fails, and falls back to the router
— which then answers `GET /slots?model=gpt120` with HTTP 400. The fallback is
recorded as a genuine discovery regression (counter +
`slots_child_port_unavailable` warning), so an unloaded-model poll is
indistinguishable from the real regression signal the parent fix
(LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC3) was built to expose.

## Evidence (measured)

- **Direct cause, reproduced from the production log**
  (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-28_10.gz`, lines 8204–8205):

  ```text
  2026-10-28 10:45:00,400 - INFO - [local] POST .../v1/chat/completions
    body={"model":"gpt120", ... "reply OK" ...} session_id=b87b8e0c-...
  2026-10-28 10:45:00,404 - WARNING - slots_child_port_unavailable: no model
    child port discovered for model=gpt120; falling back to router port 8080 ...
  ```

  The warning fires **4 ms after** the chat request and `current_model=Qwen3`
  is reported by `/status` two seconds later — i.e. the caller is the chat
  dispatch path, not a status poll.
- **Call path:** `proxy/proxy/router.py` (`_check_slot_availability` call) →
  `router_helpers._check_slot_availability()` →
  `_resolve_local_slots_target(srv, model="gpt120", ...)` →
  `_discover_local_child_port()` finds no signal for `gpt120` →
  `_warn_child_port_fallback()` increments
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  and emits the throttled WARNING, then the poll goes to the **router**.
- **Scale (from LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 window evidence):** 2,407 router-responder
  `/slots` 400 responses across the 48 h superset (243 on 2026-10-27, 2,164 on
  2026-10-28, vs 86 on 2026-10-26). The 400 side is owned by
  LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8; this item owns the *fallback-signal* side and the
  needless request.
- **Counter readings:** unreadable for the window (serving pid replaced
  2026-10-30T10:35:07Z); post-window pid 3224511 read `2` in its first
  ~8.7 h. The live pid 3944027 emitted one warning at
  `2026-10-31T00:42:00.198Z` for `model=mxbai-embed` — a **loaded** model with
  no discoverable child port, i.e. exactly the shape AC2 must keep counting.
- **Behavioural equivalence of skipping:** in `_check_slot_availability()` only
  a `200` with zero free slots produces a 503; every non-200 (including the
  router's definitive 400) already falls through to `return None`. Skipping the
  poll for a definitively unloaded model therefore **does not change the
  admission decision** — it only removes the request, the counter increment and
  the warning.

## Users and impact

- **Operator / observability consumer** — user story: *As the operator, I want
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` and the
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning to fire only when a **loaded** model's
  child port cannot be discovered, so that a real child-port discovery
  regression cannot hide behind unloaded-model noise.*
- **herdr dispatcher / capacity signal (`/llama/local/status`)** — user story:
  *As the dispatcher, I want proxy `/slots` polling to stay off the router for
  models that are not loaded, so polls do not queue behind the busy child or
  add 4xx noise to the router access log.*
- **Router access-log reader** — user story: *As an operator triaging
  `llama-server.log`, I want the router-responder `/slots` 400 population to be
  attributable to genuine external probes, not to the proxy polling for models
  that are not loaded.*

## Existing state

- All proxy-initiated `/slots` queries route through
  `_resolve_local_slots_target()` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`), which
  rewrites the local router endpoint to the discovered child port and, on
  discovery failure, calls `_warn_child_port_fallback()` (counter + throttled
  warning; LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC2/AC3).
- `_discover_local_child_port()` correctly returns `None` for a model with no
  child instance — the defect is that "no child instance because the model is
  not loaded" is treated as a *discovery failure* rather than a definitive
  non-stale answer.
- An authoritative "is this model loaded" primitive already exists:
  `srv.router_is_model_loaded()` / `srv.router_list_models()`
  (`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py:997–1075`), reading the router's `/models`
  (`status.value` = loaded/ready/running/active), with presence-with-no-status
  treated as loaded.
- `srv.current_model` is set to the loaded llama model name in router mode
  (`lifecycle.py:2383`) **but** at startup it is first set to
  `router_preload_list[0]` (`server.py:949`), which can be a non-chat preset
  (`mxbai-embed`) — see the live warning above.
- The `/health` reachability probe no longer queries `/slots`
  (LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0), which is why the residual fallback signal is now
  dominated by this chat-path case.

## Desired change (proposed; scope confirmed at intake — see Appendix)

1. **Guard before polling.** Before issuing `GET /slots?model=<m>` against the
   local router, establish whether `<m>` is loaded. When it is **definitively
   not loaded**, skip the poll entirely: no router request, no
   `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` increment, no
   `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning. There is no slot state to learn for
   a model with no instance.
2. **Keep the genuine signal.** A `/slots` poll for a **loaded** model whose
   child port cannot be discovered must still increment the counter and emit
   the throttled warning (AC2).
3. **Source of truth for "loaded".** Prefer the router's `/models` loaded set
   (existing `router_is_model_loaded()`), cached for a short TTL to keep chat
   dispatch cheap; fall back to polling (never skip) when the probe is
   unavailable or the name cannot be resolved — a false skip would remove a
   legitimate availability gate.
4. **Observability of the skip (proposed, optional).** A dedicated counter
   (e.g. `llama_slots_child_port_skipped_total{reason="model_not_loaded"}`) or
   a debug line so a skip is distinguishable from "never polled" when
   verifying AC1 on a live proxy.
5. **Docs.** `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` (observability / target-signal
   sections) and the resolver docstring plus the `proxy/README.md`
   child-port-discovery section must describe the unloaded-model skip and its
   signal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Unloaded model is not counted.** A `/slots` poll for a model that
      is not currently loaded does **not** increment
      `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
      and emits no `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning (asserted via the
      counter/warning in a test; the router is not contacted).
- [ ] **AC2 — Loaded-model regression still pinned.** A `/slots` poll for the
      loaded chat model whose child port cannot be discovered **still**
      increments the counter and emits the throttled warning (regression test,
      must fail if the guard swallows loaded-model discovery failures).
- [ ] **AC3 — `/status` capacity truth preserved.** `/status` continues to
      report truthful capacity (existing "definitive model absent" behaviour:
      fail-open on the configured pool, no resurrected fossil counts).
- [ ] **AC4 — Documentation.** `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` observability
      section and the `_resolve_local_slots_target()` /
      `_discover_local_child_port()` docstrings in
      `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` describe the unloaded-model skip; the
      `proxy/README.md` child-port-discovery section agrees.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full suite green.** Full project test suite passes with the
      change (run through the test skill; changed-scope gate first).
- [ ] **AC6 — Skip is observable (proposed).** Live/`/metrics` evidence
      distinguishes a skipped poll from a poll that was never attempted (new
      counter or documented log line), so AC1 can be verified post-deploy.
- [ ] **AC7 — Admission outcome unchanged.** A test pins that skipping the
      availability check for an unloaded model returns the same admission
      result (`None`) as the current definitive-400 fall-through — the fix must
      not start refusing or blocking requests.

## Constraints

- **No new router `/slots` traffic** and no new blocking call on the chat hot
  path: any "is it loaded" probe must be cheap and cached (`/models` only, not
  `/slots`).
- **Fail open, never fail closed:** when loadedness cannot be determined, poll
  as today. A wrong skip would remove a real availability gate and allow
  over-subscription of the slot pool.
- `_resolve_local_slots_target()` is **synchronous** while
  `router_is_model_loaded()` is **async** — the guard must live at the async
  call site(s) (or use a pre-fetched cached loaded set), not inside the
  resolver, unless the resolver is given the loaded set as an argument.
- `_discover_local_child_port()` semantics stay unchanged (a missing signal is
  still "no port"); the definitive "model not loaded" classification is layered
  above it.
- Do not weaken the LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC3 guarantee for the loaded model.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — add the unloaded-model guard at the async
  `_check_slot_availability()` call site (and `_resolve_local_slots_target()`
  docs/metric plumbing); keep `_warn_child_port_fallback()` for loaded models.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — reuse `router_is_model_loaded()` /
  `router_list_models()`; add a short-TTL loaded-set cache (router pid keyed)
  if the guard needs one.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `poll_slots_for_model()` (the per-model poller
  resolves through the same path and must obey the same skip rule).
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — fallback counter (unchanged) plus, if AC6 is
  accepted, the `skipped` counter.
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_query_target_call_sites.py` — extend the shared
  resolver/call-site suite.
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_unloaded_model_skip.py` — new focused tests for
  AC1/AC2/AC7 (unloaded skip, loaded-model regression pinned, admission
  outcome unchanged).
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_availability_dedicated_client.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_child_port_discovery_rotation.py` — verify the guard did
  not disturb existing availability/discovery contracts.
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` — observability + "target signal going
  forward" sections.
- `proxy/README.md` — "Child-port discovery" / fallback-observability section.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF** — *Residual router-proxied `/slots` 500s: audit
  remaining call sites and enforce direct child-port polling* (done). Parent of
  the shared resolver, counter and throttled warning this item refines.
- **LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8** — *Router `/slots` HTTP 400s: `?model=` resolution
  path* (plan_complete). Owns the 400-response side; its intake answer Q2=A
  established that a `?model=<unloaded>` 400 is *expected truth* — this item
  removes the proxy's **own** such polls without changing that stance. Its
  six slices (all `intake_complete`, blocked) overlap in two concrete places:
  - **LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** — *Resolve the model id from `/models` instead of
    hard-coding Qwen3* (slice 4). Delivers a **TTL-cached `/models` id
    snapshot** that the unloaded-model guard should reuse rather than
    duplicate (see Appendix Q2/Q3).
  - **LP-0MVU7ZZ7M002D9GT** — *Thread the resolved model through the
    model-less `/slots` probes* (slice 3). Its "skip the query when no model is
    known" is a **different** condition (empty model name) from this item's
    "model known but not loaded" — no AC overlap, but the same call sites.
  - **LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL** — *Document the model-resolution rule and 400
    semantics* (slice 5) touches the same `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`
    section AC4 edits here — sequence or coordinate to avoid a doc conflict.
- **LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12** — *Static audit: enumerate every `/slots` 400 call
  path* (child of LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8, intake_complete). Shares the call-site
  inventory this item needs.
- **LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0** — *Proxy `/health` reachability probe polls router
  `GET /slots?model=`* (completed). Removed the previously dominant
  fallback/500 source; that is why the chat-path case is now the visible one.
- **LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57** — *Verify `router:500 == 0` over 24 h after the
  child-port discovery fix*. Supplies the window evidence quoted above.
- **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** — *False "saturated" capacity signal starves herdr
  downtime dispatcher* (completed). Source of the definitive-model-absent /
  fail-open contract that AC3 and AC7 must preserve.
- **LP-0MTP1FQXH004JYEF** — model-filtered child-port discovery (`mxbai-embed`
  vs `Qwen3`), i.e. the reason a model name is passed to discovery at all.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (high impact): false "not loaded" ⇒ a real availability gate is
  skipped** and the pool can be over-subscribed. *Mitigation:* require an
  explicit `not loaded` answer from the router's `/models`; fail open to
  polling on any probe error; AC2 + AC7 tests pin both directions.
- **Risk: extra `/models` call per chat dispatch.** *Mitigation:* short-TTL
  cached loaded set (seconds, keyed on router pid), refreshed on miss; measure
  nothing new on the hot path beyond one cache lookup.
- **Risk: name aliasing** (client model id ≠ llama model name ≠ router preset
  id). *Mitigation:* compare the already-resolved llama model name
  (`_resolve_slot_model_name`) case-insensitively; treat "unknown/not present"
  as *not* evidence of unloaded and poll as today.
- **Risk: `srv.current_model` is not a reliable loaded-set** (startup pins it
  to `router_preload_list[0]`, live example `mxbai-embed`; router mode can hold
  several loaded models). *Mitigation:* `/models` is the authority; treat
  `current_model` as a fallback only, and never as proof of absence.
- **Assumption:** the admission outcome for an unloaded model is unchanged
  because the current definitive-400 path already returns `None`
  (`_check_slot_availability` only 503s on `200` with zero free slots).
- **Assumption:** "not loaded" polls carry no information for capacity
  signalling, so deleting them cannot degrade `/status` (which polls
  `srv.current_model`, i.e. a model it believes is loaded).
- **Scope-creep risk:** the startup `current_model = router_preload_list[0]`
  behaviour (and the resulting `mxbai-embed` warning) is a *separate* defect
  about loaded-model bookkeeping. Record as a linked follow-up rather than
  widening this item (see Appendix Q3).

## Out of scope

- Eliminating router `/slots` 400 responses in general (LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8)
  and the new per-query instrumentation deferred to LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5.
- `/health` reachability probing (already fixed in LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0).
- Changing `_discover_local_child_port()`'s discovery sources or caching.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded 2026-10-31 during the intake session for
LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K (agent: Map). All three are **OPEN QUESTION** — the item
was explicitly filed with "scope to confirm at intake", so no answer has been
assumed.

- **Q1 — How wide is the skip?**
  - **A)** Guard **every** proxy-initiated `/slots` poll through the single
    shared path, so no proxy surface can poll a definitively unloaded model
    (chat-dispatch availability check, per-model poller, status/SSE paths —
    the latter two only matter if their model argument can be a non-loaded
    name).
  - **B)** Guard **only** the chat-dispatch availability check
    (`_check_slot_availability`) that produced the `gpt120` evidence; leave the
    other call sites untouched.
  - **C)** Guard the two async poller call sites only
    (`_check_slot_availability` + `poll_slots_for_model`), leaving the
    status/SSE paths alone.
  - **Recommended: A** — the ACs are written at the resolver level, and a
    single guard prevents a future call site from re-introducing the noise;
    the status/SSE paths pass `srv.current_model` today, so A costs them
    nothing in the common case.
  - **Answer:** *OPEN QUESTION — pending producer.*

- **Q2 — What is the authority for "currently loaded"?**
  - **A)** `srv.current_model` only (cheapest, already in hand; but it is
    pinned to `router_preload_list[0]` at startup and router mode can hold
    several loaded models, so it can neither prove absence nor list the loaded
    set).
  - **B)** The router's `/models` loaded set (existing
    `router_is_model_loaded()` / `router_list_models()`), behind a short-TTL
    cached snapshot; poll as today whenever the probe fails or the name is
    unresolved.
  - **C)** Hybrid: `srv.current_model` fast path, confirm with a `/models`
    probe before *skipping* (never skip on `current_model` alone).
  - **D)** Defer the mechanism to implementation: require only that a skip
    happens solely on a positive "not loaded" answer from a cached
    `/models` snapshot, reusing LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW's snapshot when it lands.
  - **Recommended: B (or D if the producer prefers no mechanism commitment at
    intake)** — `/models` is the authoritative loaded set, the primitive
    already exists, and the probe is a cached local call; C would still need
    the `/models` probe on the skip path, so B is the same safety with less
    branching. Whichever is chosen, the guard must **never** skip on
    `current_model` disagreement alone (live counter-example: startup pins it
    to `mxbai-embed`).
  - **Answer:** *OPEN QUESTION — pending producer.*

- **Q3 — Sequencing against the sibling 400s item.**
  - **A)** Land independently now as a narrow proxy-side skip; leave
    LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8's "a `?model=<unloaded>` 400 is expected truth,
    documented not eliminated" decision untouched (accepting a small
    `/models`-cache duplication with LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW and a possible doc
    merge with LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL).
  - **B)** Block on the sibling slices that supply the pieces —
    **LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** (cached `/models` id snapshot) and
    **LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL** (the `slots-500-triage.md` documentation section)
    — then land this item on top, reusing both.
  - **C)** Keep this item's ACs as they are but record a soft dependency
    ("reuse if landed; implement locally otherwise") instead of a hard blocker.
  - **Recommended: B for the *mechanism* dependency, A for the *AC* scope** —
    i.e. no change to what this item must prove, but schedule it after
    LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW so the `/models` snapshot and the doc section are not
    built twice (the sibling chain is already blocked and moving).
  - **Answer:** *OPEN QUESTION — pending producer.*

**Research summary (agent):** the chat-request → availability-check →
resolver → counter/warning chain was confirmed line-by-line against the
production log (2026-10-28T10:45:00.400Z `gpt120` POST → 10:45:00.404Z
warning, `current_model=Qwen3` at 10:45:02). The authoritative loaded-set
primitive (`router_is_model_loaded()`) already exists and was confirmed by
inspection (`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py:997–1075`). Skipping the poll is
behaviourally equivalent to the current definitive-400 fall-through in
`_check_slot_availability()`, so AC7 is a safety pin, not a new behaviour.
A duplicate-work sweep found **no** item that already satisfies AC1–AC3: the
sibling chain LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 → {LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12,
LP-0MVU7ZZ7M002D9GT, LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW, LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL,
LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8, LP-0MVU7ZYWS002RDYM} covers model-less / hard-coded
`?model=` 400s, not "model known but not loaded" — but two slices supply
pieces this item would otherwise rebuild (cached `/models` snapshot; the same
doc section), which is what Q3 asks the producer to sequence.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** – Resolve the model id from /models instead of hard-coding Qwen3 (AC2 part 2, AC3b) (blocked)
- **LP-0MNA7FYH4001ZUR4** – Router-mode llama-server integration (completed)
- **LP-0MQB9JR38002PFIL** – Extract model lifecycle helpers to lifecycle.py (completed)

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+459 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+459 more)

# Intake Brief — Early-released local dispatch keeps prefilling in `llama-server` and starves the next dispatch

## Problem statement

The Option D early release (LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN) detours the client in under a
second, but it does not demonstrably stop the work it abandoned at
`llama-server`: in the measured 24 h window **285 of 1 092 backend prompt
evaluations (26 %) were never consumed by a proxy stream**, and **58 of 60**
residual `prefill_deadline` evictions started inside an *estimated*
abandoned-prefill window. Each fake-warm dispatch therefore appears to cost a
release *plus* a 120 s residual: the retry — which returns to the same
session-pinned slot — reports no prefill progress for its whole lease and is
evicted in turn.

The premise cannot be taken as given. Intake-time log inspection
(2026-10-31, current `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log`) found 143
`Connection handling canceled` events, of which 49 could be joined to a task
id; **only 4 were followed by any further `prompt processing progress` line,
each at most one batch**, and none reached `prompt eval time` after the
cancel. The upstream cancel implemented by LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB does take
effect — so the *magnitude* (26 % of compute, 667 s median backlog) and the
*mechanism* (abandoned work runs to completion) must be decided on evidence
before a fix is chosen. That decision is AC1.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Owns the prefill-deadline and eviction metrics
  and pays for cloud fallback; needs the 26 % waste and the 1.96 user-class
  evictions/h explained and reduced, and needs the residual counts to stop
  being re-attributed every measurement cycle.
- **Agent sessions (herdr workers, `pi` sessions).** They are the retries: a
  dispatch starved behind abandoned work ends as a 503 detour, a longer
  latency, or a failed audit run.
- **Measurement analyst.** Re-runs
  `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py`; needs each release
  joined to the backend task it cancelled, so "prefills computed and thrown
  away" is a measurement and not the subtraction of two unrelated counters.

User stories:

- As an operator, when the proxy releases an accepted local dispatch early, I
  want the GPU work it abandoned to stop within a bounded, recorded time — and
  I want to see that bound in the logs — so compute is never thrown away
  silently.
- As an agent session, when my request is retried after an early release, I
  want it either to prefill immediately (on a free slot) or not to be admitted
  at all, rather than burn a 120 s lease with zero measured progress.
- As an analyst, I want the abandoned-prefill estimate to state its own
  provenance and error, so the 58/60 and 26 % figures are either confirmed or
  restated with evidence rather than quoted as fact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Mechanism decided (confirmed or refuted) with recorded evidence.**
  A committed record under `docs/dev/` (for example
  `docs/dev/abandoned-prefill-release-cancel.md`) reports, for a ≥24 h window,
  per post-acceptance release: release reason, proxy release timestamp, joined
  backend task id (where a join exists), whether a backend cancel was observed,
  the number of `prompt processing progress` lines after the cancel, the time
  from cancel to `slot release: … stop processing`, and whether a
  `prompt eval time` line was emitted for that task. The record states a
  verdict for each competing mechanism below, with the log lines that decide
  it, and either confirms or restates the 26 % (285/1 092) and 58/60 figures:
  - **H1 — the abandoned prefill runs to completion.** Discriminator: cancel
    events followed by many progress batches, and `prompt eval time` emitted
    for a cancelled task. *Intake sample argues against this (4 of 49, ≤1
    batch each) — it must still be measured over 24 h, not assumed.*
  - **H2 — the cancel lands only at a batch boundary.** Discriminator:
    cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution against observed
    `batch.n_tokens` (up to 8 192) at the measured prompt-eval rate (current
    log p10/p50/p90 = 86 / 158 / 536 tok/s), i.e. a bounded tail of roughly
    6–52 s rather than minutes.
  - **H3 — the 26 % is an accounting artefact.** Discriminator: reconcile
    `prompt eval time` (backend, *all* consumers) against
    `Stream finished … provider=local` (proxy) per hour, and enumerate
    non-proxy consumers of `llama-server` (direct calls in `scripts/`,
    benchmarks, health probes) that would be counted as "thrown away".
  - **H4 — the retry is queued behind a draining slot.** Discriminator:
    `slot launch_slot_` time for the retry task versus the abandoned task's
    `slot release`, joined through the proxy's session→slot assignment
    (`_slot_id_for_session` keeps a session on its slot, so a retry returns to
    the slot it abandoned).
  - **H5 — the residual is capacity, not starvation.** Discriminator: the
    event's prompt size and measured prompt-eval rate against the 120 s
    deadline (median event is a 78 213-token prompt; at 158 tok/s a full
    re-prefill is ≈495 s, at 536 tok/s ≈146 s), and whether any later dispatch
    of the same prompt ever reached `progress = 1.0`.

- **AC2 — The release's effect on the backend is bounded and observable.** A
  committed analyser (extend
  `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` or add a sibling)
  joins proxy post-acceptance releases to backend task lifecycles over a ≥24 h
  window and emits: releases with no observed backend cancel (count and
  share), the cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution, and the tokens
  actually evaluated after the cancel. Every release whose cancel cannot be
  joined is reported as unjoined rather than dropped. Target (assumption to
  confirm): **≤ 5 % of releases with no explained backend stop**, and a
  recorded p90 stop latency bound.

- **AC3 — The next dispatch is not starved by abandoned work.** In a
  post-change ≥24 h window (restart-segmented, from on-disk logs), the share
  of `prefill_deadline` events whose dispatch start falls inside an
  abandoned-prefill window falls from **58/60** to a recorded target
  (assumption: **≤ 20 %**), **and** no accepted dispatch expires its lease
  with zero `prefill_progress_measured` while its session's slot is still
  draining an abandoned task — either the retry is routed to a free slot, or
  it observes prefill progress inside its lease. Both halves must be reported;
  a bare `prefill_deadline` count can be gamed by reason conversion (248
  `measured_cache_deficit` releases in the same window).

- **AC4 — No warm-path or throughput regression.** Against the matched
  pre-change window: local completions per hour and large-warm completion
  latency (p50/p90) are not reduced, and `measured_cache_deficit` releases per
  hour do not rise, measured per
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md`. Both windows are reported, with the
  deltas, not just a verdict.

- **AC5 — Tests and documentation.** Hermetic tests pin the new
  release→cancel accounting and any routing/accounting behaviour change (no
  live `llama-server` dependency). Documentation is updated to reflect the
  change, including code comments, `proxy/docs/routing.md` (the abandoned
  dispatch section), `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`, the
  `abandoned_prefill_windows()` docstring in the analyser (which currently
  asserts the opposite of `routing.md`), and
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md` where the baseline moves. The full
  project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Out of scope (owned elsewhere, do not re-tune):** the prefill deadline
  (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds=120`), the cold-prefill budget
  (`local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens=25000`), the admission ladder's warmth
  pricing (LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27), and the slot count (LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5).
- **`llama-server` exposes no cancel API.** Cancellation is only observable as
  a closed socket, and the backend acts on it at its next socket write, so the
  effective granularity is one `n_batch` (up to 8 192 tokens observed). Any
  batch-size (`-ub`/`--batch-size`) change is a backend-config change and must
  be justified by AC1 evidence as a recorded decision — not tuned silently in
  this item.
- **No overlap with the annotation work.** LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM and its child
  LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK own the abandoned-slot identity/annotation
  (`abandoned_busy`, registry entries on every release path, including the
  Option D path's missing `abandoned_slot_id`); this item owns the
  *behaviour* — does the backend stop, and is the next dispatch starved.
  Implementation must not duplicate or contradict that annotation, and the
  Option D plumbing gap is reported to those items rather than fixed here.
- **Measurement integrity.** `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S = 43.1` in the
  analyser prices the abandoned backlog; the measured prompt-eval rate on the
  current log is p10 86 / p50 158 / p90 536 tok/s, so the 667 s median backlog
  estimate is likely overstated several-fold. Any correction must be recorded
  as a measurement change with its own evidence, and the 58/60 figure restated
  on both the old and the corrected basis (backwards comparable) rather than
  swapped.
- **Measurement windows** are ≥24 h, restart-segmented, derived from on-disk
  logs only (no in-process counters), per the existing
  `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md` method.

## Existing state

- **The upstream cancel already exists.** LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (with
  LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK) made every abandonment path close the captured upstream
  stream through `_release_unserved_dispatch`, and records the abandoned slot
  identity for the status annotation. `proxy/docs/routing.md` claims the
  cancel is real: 42 of 82 `Connection handling canceled` events on 2026-10-28
  cancelled a task that never reached `prompt processing done`.
- **The Option D path does not use that plumbing.** In `proxy/proxy/router.py`
  the `MeasuredCacheAbortDetourError` handler calls
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch(...)` **without**
  `upstream_stream_cm` or `abandoned_slot_id` (the deadline path at
  `router.py:2220` passes `upstream_stream_cm=cm`), then closes the stream and
  client itself. So the 42/82 evidence was taken on a different code path than
  the one that produces most of the 389 post-acceptance releases, and the
  abandoned-slot annotation is not recorded for the Option D releases (that
  annotation gap is LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK's scope; here it is evidence, not
  work).
- **The analyser's model contradicts `routing.md`.**
  `abandoned_prefill_windows()` documents "A released dispatch is **not**
  cancelled at `llama-server`" and prices the *whole* remaining prompt
  (`tokens / 43.1`) as backend occupancy — the source of the 667 s median and
  of the 58/60 overlap figure.
- **Session→slot affinity makes the retry return to the draining slot.**
  `_slot_id_for_session` (`proxy/proxy/session.py`) keeps a session on its
  assigned slot, so the immediate retry after a 503 targets the same slot the
  release just abandoned. `slot_id=unknown` on every post-F4 eviction line
  means slot-level attribution is currently unavailable from the eviction log
  alone (it must be reconstructed from `launch_slot_`/`slot release` pairs).
- **Current live counts (intake sample).** `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`
  (3.7 h, 2026-10-31 00:41 → 04:21) holds 39 `local_eviction_after_acceptance`
  events; `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` holds 143 cancels, 121
  completed prompt evaluations and 34 batches of 8 192 tokens.
- **Queue-wait work overlaps but is a different question.**
  LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR / LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5 diagnose why *queue* waits expire
  at the 60 s budget (blocker class, guard projection); this item is about
  accepted dispatches starved by abandoned work they were never told about.

## Desired change

1. Decide H1–H5 on 24 h evidence and publish the decision record (AC1), with
   the 26 % / 58-of-60 claims confirmed or restated.
2. Make the release's backend effect attributable per dispatch (AC2), so
   "abandoned" stops being an estimate derived from a token-rate constant.
3. Remove the starvation path found by AC1 — at minimum: a retry must never be
   admitted into a slot that is still draining work the proxy itself abandoned
   without that fact being visible to admission and to the eviction log
   (AC3). The specific mechanism (route to a free slot, hold the dispatch out
   of "about to prefill" pricing, or bound the wait against the drain) is a
   decision for AC1's evidence, not for intake.
4. Prove no warm-path or throughput regression (AC4), and leave the
   documentation and tests consistent with the new measurement (AC5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — the `MeasuredCacheAbortDetourError` handler
  (≈ lines 1998–2120) and the deadline handler (≈ lines 2190–2260); the Option
  D release currently omits `upstream_stream_cm` / `abandoned_slot_id`.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`, `_record_abandoned_slot`,
  `_abandoned_slot_lookup`.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_slot_id_for_session` / `_slot_owners` (session
  affinity is what sends the retry back to the draining slot).
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` —
  `abandoned_prefill_windows()`, `backend_prefill_accounting()`,
  `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S`.
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`,
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — the three
  records whose claims must agree after the change.
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_measured_cache_abort*.py` — the existing hermetic
  coverage the new tests sit beside.

## Related work

- LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O — the measurement item that produced the 26 % / 58-of-60
  evidence (`discovered-from` parent of this item).
- LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (completed) and LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK (completed) — the
  upstream cancel + abandoned-slot registry whose effectiveness this item
  re-verifies for the Option D path.
- LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2 (completed) — regression test: abandoned dispatch not
  reported saturated.
- LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM (in progress) — annotate the post-cancel release lag so a
  draining slot is never reported saturated. Adjacent, not overlapping.
- LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK (blocked) — record and re-verify abandoned slot identity
  on every release path (including the unattributable
  `measured_cache_deficit` polls). Owns the annotation gap this item records as
  evidence.
- LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN — Option D early release (the release under test).
- LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 — warmth pricing (out of scope here).
- LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5 — slot count (out of scope here).
- LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR, LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5, LP-0MVV29X2E004INFL — abandoned
  *queue-wait* share diagnosis; same abandonments, different question.
- LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK — post-deadline re-dispatch fix measurement window (its
  restart precondition applies here too: a post-change window needs the proxy
  restarted onto the fix).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (AC3 target):** ≤ 20 % of `prefill_deadline` events starting
  inside an abandoned-prefill window, plus zero zero-progress starvations.
  Chosen because a hard zero cannot be promised while the backend's stop
  granularity is one batch; confirm at review.
- **Assumption (AC2 target):** ≤ 5 % of releases with no explained backend
  stop. Confirm at review.
- **Assumption (scope):** a `--batch-size` change is out of scope for the fix
  and, if AC1 shows the batch tail dominates, is recorded as a follow-up work
  item rather than tuned here.
- **Assumption (refutation path):** if AC1 refutes H1 and the 26 % proves to be
  an accounting artefact, this item stays open and re-scopes to the mechanism
  the evidence supports (H3 + H4/H5); the refutation plus the corrected
  estimator is the deliverable, and the item is not closed on the refutation
  alone.
- **Risk — stale evidence transfer.** The 42/82 cancel evidence was taken on
  the deadline path, not the Option D path; AC1 must not reuse it as proof.
- **Risk — reason conversion games the metric.** A reduction in
  `prefill_deadline` can be produced by more `measured_cache_deficit` releases;
  AC3 therefore counts both reasons and AC4 bounds the latter.
- **Risk — measurement window invalidated by a restart.** A post-change window
  requires the proxy to be restarted onto the fix; if it is not, the window
  measures the old code (the exact failure recorded in LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Batch-size tuning, deadline/budget re-tuning, warmth
  pricing, slot-count changes and queue-budget modelling are all *linked work
  items*, never extra scope here.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: What numeric target counts as "the next dispatch is not starved"
  (AC3)?** — *Not asked interactively; no blocking answer required.*
  **Default adopted at intake:** ≤ 20 % of `prefill_deadline` events starting
  inside an abandoned-prefill window, plus zero dispatches expiring with no
  `prefill_progress_measured` while their slot drains abandoned work.
  Source: intake reasoning from the measured 58/60 baseline and the
  batch-granularity constraint (a hard zero is unprovable while the backend
  stops only at a batch boundary). Producer may adjust at review.
- **Q: Is a `llama-server` batch-size (`-ub`/`--batch-size`) change in scope
  if AC1 shows the batch tail dominates the waste?** — **Default adopted at
  intake:** out of scope for this item's fix; recorded as a decision in AC1 and
  filed as a follow-up work item if the evidence supports it. Source: the
  item's own scope note ("make the release cancel or bound the abandoned
  backend work") plus the standing rule against re-tuning deployed knobs
  without new evidence.
- **Q: If AC1 refutes the "prefill runs to completion" premise, does this item
  close on the refutation?** — **Default adopted at intake:** no; the item
  re-scopes to the mechanism the evidence supports and keeps AC3's starvation
  target as the closure gate. Source: the item already frames AC1 as
  "confirmed or refuted", and a refutation that leaves 1.96 user-class
  evictions/h unexplained would leave the operator's question unanswered.
- **Research note (duplicate check).** `wl search prefill`, `wl search
  "abandoned prefill"`, `wl search cancel`, `wl search starv` and
  `wl search ghost` were run. No completed item satisfies this item's ACs:
  LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB implemented the cancel but did not verify it per
  dispatch or address the starved retry; LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM annotates the
  draining slot but does not change behaviour. The description was therefore
  re-scoped to the *difference*: per-dispatch cancel accounting, the Option D
  path's missing plumbing, and the starvation of the retry.
- **Research note (log sample, 2026-10-31).** `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log`:
  143 `Connection handling canceled`, 49 joinable to a task id, 4 with any
  `prompt processing progress` after the cancel (≤ 1 batch each), 121
  `prompt eval time` lines, 34 batches of `batch.n_tokens = 8192`; prompt-eval
  rate p10/p50/p90 = 86 / 158 / 536 tok/s. `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`
  (3.7 h) holds 39 `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events. Method: `grep`
  plus a task-id join script over the live log; reproducible from the log
  files named above.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK** – Record and re-verify abandoned slot identity on every release path (blocked)
- **LP-0MSB0RV72001KNRV** – Slot registry leak: _cleanup_stale_local_dispatch never frees _slot_owners entries (completed)
- **LP-0MQS6MPWE005NJJA** – Phase 3: Session invalidation → slot release (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: abort, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+436 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: abort, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+436 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: abort, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+436 more)

# Writer-side sidecar still absent at seed time post-fix — 0 found/restored over ≥24 h (LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB verdict)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the restored-prefix credit to actually fire (and,
secondarily, the snapshot/sidecar pair to stay coupled on disk), so that AC3
of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E can be answered with non-zero restored dispatches and
`found` seeds.

## Background (evidence, 2026-10-30)

The verification item LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB measured a ≥24 h post-fix window
(fix `5502ee44`, deployed 2026-10-29T12:58:32Z) and found the expected
signature absent:

- `cache_state=restored` dispatches: **0**; `slot_ratio_restored` events: **0**;
  `outcome=found` seeds: **0** (unchanged from the 155 h / 4,488-decision baseline).
- Seed outcomes shifted the wrong way: `missing_sidecar` 303 → **605** (98.1 % of
  617), `missing_snapshot` 392 → 12; guard outcomes still 0 (guard never reached).
- Writer-side health worsened: router-path slot saves 103/33 ok/fail (24 % fail)
  pre-fix → 34/65 (66 % fail) post-fix; eviction saves 9/33 → 42/64;
  `persistence skipped reason=slot_busy` 155 → 260. `ReadTimeout` dominates the
  failures (52 of 106 `slot_save` failures in-window).
- AC6 pairing at report time: 0 snapshots / 28 sidecars (all orphan, all saved
  post-deploy 04:02–19:01Z on 10-30) — no snapshot+sidecar pair on disk and
  orphan growth for post-deploy saves persists, 142 → 28 legacy orphans cleared.

Reproducible data: `docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-2026-10-30.json` (+
`-full.json`), source logs `/var/log/llama-proxy` (`slot_ratio_seed outcome=…`,
`slot_save …`, `slot persistence skipped …`).

## Hypotheses to test (from the verdict)

1. **Eviction-sidecar write skipped.** `session._write_eviction_sidecar`
   returns early when `provider.get_recorded_prompt_prefix(model, session_id)`
   is `None` — sessions whose measured prefix was never recorded (e.g. usage
   block missing prompt_tokens, or prefix cleared) get a snapshot with **no**
   sidecar, which later seeds as `missing_sidecar`. Audit-traffic sessions
   dominate the 605 hits. Quantify how many eviction `saved=True` events are
   followed by a sidecar appearing on disk vs not, by session.
2. **Router-sidecar write skipped on 0-token fallback.**
   `provider.sidecar_cached_tokens` returns 0 (no usage, no recorded prefix,
   empty-message estimate fail) → the router writes no sidecar. Confirm the
   fallback estimate (`_estimate_prompt_tokens_for_routing`) can return 0 for
   real prompt shapes.
3. **Save/retire path divergence producing orphan sidecars.** A sidecar survives
   its snapshot (opposite of the AC3 coupling) — e.g. save resolves an endpoint
   dir path (`localhost-8080/`) while `_invalidate_session_and_slot` retires a
   root-style path, or `slot_id` vs `session_id` filename mismatch. Reproduce
   minimally and fix the divergence; the daily `cleanup-slot-cache.sh` removes
   pairs/orphans only, it never creates a survivor, so the proxy itself leaves
   them.
4. **Save-failure cliff.** 66 % router-save failure (`ReadTimeout`, `slot_busy`
   skip growth) starves the sidecar supply. Triage whether this is a timeout
   tuning, concurrency, or llama-server-side regression independent of the seed
   path.

## Acceptance criteria

- A minimal repro or direct log evidence pins which write path produced each
  observed `missing_sidecar` snapshot (router vs eviction), with counts for at
  least the 24 h post-fix window.
- Root cause identified and fixed so that a snapshot saved post-fix is paired
  with a sidecar (AC6-style pairing check: paired files present, no orphan
  growth for post-deploy saves).
- Post-fix ≥24 h window after the NEW deploy shows `outcome=found` > 0 and
  `cache_state=restored` dispatches > 0 (matching LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E AC3), or
  a documented, evidence-backed explanation of why the credit cannot fire with
  the current guard/prefix semantics.
- Verdict recorded in `docs/dev/` with exact command line and JSON artifact
  mirroring LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB.

## Notes

- discovered-from: LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB (which superseded LP-0MVK0E8NH007XCV3).
- The AC3 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E remains unmet until this item closes.
- Do not "fix" a non-zero `prefix_mismatch`/`expired` if one appears — those
  guard outcomes are the *success* signal that the seed path runs past lookup
  (LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3); if they dominate, reopen the guard question with
  counts.

## Objective (user story)

As the proxy maintainer, I want the router-responder `GET /slots ... 500` count
measured over a clean 24 h production window **after** the `/health`
reachability-probe fix (LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0) is deployed, so that the
`router:500 == 0` regression signal is either proven restored (verdict
**GREEN**) or the residual cause is named and filed (verdict **RED**).

## Problem statement

LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0 removes `GET /slots?model=<current>` from
`_probe_backend_reachable()`'s router-mode probe list (leaving `/models` +
`/health`), because `/health` calls that probe on every request and each
router-proxied `/slots` probe can be answered `500` when the router's proxied
poll is cancelled by a busy child. Unit tests can prove that no router `/slots`
request is issued, but only a post-deploy production window proves the
windowed count is actually `0` — that is AC3 of the fix item and it cannot be
satisfied before deployment.

## Existing state (verified at intake, 2026-10-30T23:30Z)

**The fix is not in production yet — this item is measurement-blocked, not
code-blocked.**

- Main checkout still has the pre-fix code:
  `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py::_probe_backend_reachable()` builds
  `probe_paths = ["/slots?model=<current_model>", "/models", "/health"]` when
  `llama_router_mode` is set.
- The fix exists only as **uncommitted work in progress** in the sibling
  worktree
  `.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0-proxy-health-reachability-probe-polls-ro`
  (branch of the same name; `M docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`,
  `M proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`, untracked
  `proxy/tests/test_health_probe_router_slots.py`). LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0 itself
  is `status: open`, `stage: plan_complete` — not committed, not merged, not
  on `main`.
- Deployed proxy: pid **3797968**, `lstart` **Fri Oct 30 23:10:47 2026 (UTC)**,
  `cwd` = `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy` → the **pre-fix** code.
- **Live reproduction (read-only, 3 requests):** `curl -s -o /dev/null
  localhost:8000/health` ×3 at 2026-10-30T23:30Z appended exactly 3
  `GET /slots` lines to `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` — child
  `[35443] ... 200` plus **2 router-responder `500`s** (lines with no `[pid]`
  prefix). One health check ⇒ one router `/slots` request, as documented.
- Pre-fix baseline, 2026-10-30 (live file `llama-server.log-2026-10-30`,
  00:00Z → 23:30Z, `scripts/slots_500_triage.py --summary`):
  router 200 / 400 / 500 = **434 / 1,861 / 604**; child 200s =
  53,526 (pid 35443) + 12,768 (pid 42051) + 2 (other pids); child 400/500 =
  0 / 0. Daily router-500 trend (same recipe): 2026-10-27 **128**,
  2026-10-28 **1,043**, 2026-10-29 **604**, 2026-10-30 (partial, to 23:30Z)
  **604** — the same file read **140** at ~19:00Z when
  `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` was last updated, so the residual rate is
  live, not historical.
- Live counters on the deployed (pre-fix) process at 2026-10-30T23:30Z:
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"} 1.0`,
  `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="timeout"} 115.0`.

## Why it matters

- `router:500 == 0` is the regression target recorded for the child-port
  fix and re-stated in `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` ("Target signal going
  forward"): until the `/health` probe stops polling the router, router
  `/slots` 500s are indistinguishable from a genuine polling regression.
- Each probe `/slots` also serialises behind a busy child, so `/health`
  latency degrades under prefill (same defect class as
  LP-0MTDGBRPU003Z7KU) — a secondary motivation, not an AC here.

## Desired change

Measurement + evidence only (no code change expected):

1. Run the documented 24 h post-fix window recipe against
   `llama-server*.log` / `proxy.log*`.
2. Record the verdict **GREEN** (router-responder `/slots` 500 count = 0,
   superset-scoped) or **RED** (non-zero; linked bug filed per AC4) with raw
   counts, commands and timestamps in a work-item comment.
3. Append a dated **"Post-fix 24 h window verification (`/health` probe fix,
   LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0)"** section to `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`, mirroring
   the LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 section, with a JSON sidecar in `docs/dev/` (same
   shape as `router-slots-500-window-2026-10-27-to-28.json`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Zero router 500s.** Router-responder `GET /slots ... 500` count
      is **0** across the window's `llama-server*.log` file set (superset
      scoping per the recorded recipe; a zero superset count proves zero
      in-window).
- [ ] **AC2 — Matrix recorded.** The router/child 200/400/500 matrix, the
      `slots_stale` share and the fallback signals
      (`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` counter delta, or the throttled
      `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning lines when the delta is
      unreadable) are recorded verbatim in a work-item comment.
- [ ] **AC3 — Restart integrity.** The serving proxy's pid and `lstart` are
      recorded, the window start/end timestamps are stated, and any
      in-window proxy restart is reported (with the counter delta declared
      unavailable if one occurred).
- [ ] **AC4 — Non-zero ⇒ RED + linked bug.** If the count is **not** 0, a bug
      is filed with `discovered-from:LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0` naming the responder
      split and the attributed cause, and this item's verdict is recorded as
      **RED** with the evidence linked.
- [ ] **AC5 — Repro recorded.** Repro commands, window timestamps and raw
      counts are recorded (comment + JSON sidecar).
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` gains the
      dated post-fix window section (verdict, matrix, method, limitations) and
      the JSON sidecar is committed alongside it; the "Target signal going
      forward" paragraph is updated to say whether `router:500 == 0` is now
      trustworthy.
- [ ] **AC7 — Test gate.** The change is evidence/docs only; the project test
      gate for the changed scope must pass (`build → test → commit`) before
      the commit that carries the evidence.

## Method (reuse the recorded recipe)

Recipe source: `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` §"Post-fix 24 h window
verification (LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57)" and its JSON sidecar
`docs/dev/router-slots-500-window-2026-10-27-to-28.json`.

1. **Gate: fix deployed.** Window may not start until (a) the fix is committed
   and merged to `dev`, (b) promoted `dev → main`, and (c) the proxy is
   restarted onto that build (`/skill:start-proxy --restart`). Record that
   restart's pid + `lstart` as the *deploy anchor*.
2. **Window.** Start = deploy anchor + **≥ 24 h**; end = start + 24 h (no
   restart inside). Record both timestamps in UTC.
3. **Scope.** `llama-server` access lines carry **no timestamps**, so scope by
   file: include `llama-server*.log*` files whose mtime falls in the window
   (logrotate `copytruncate` names each file by its rotation date and it
   contains the previous 24 h, so the window straddles two files = a ±12 h
   superset). `proxy.log` **is** timestamped and self-rotates every 6 h —
   filter those files by their own observed first/last timestamp.
4. **Count, per file:**
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
     --llama-file 'llama-server.log-<rotation-date>.gz' --summary
   ```
   Repeat for each in-window file; sum `responder_status.router:500` for AC1.
5. **`slots_stale` share.** From the in-window `proxy.log*` files:
   `status_request` lines with `slots_stale` / all `status_request` lines
   (primary figure), plus the active-prefill subset (secondary).
6. **Restart integrity + fallbacks.** `ps -o pid,lstart -p <pid>`; grep the
   window's `proxy.log*` for `Starting LLama Proxy Server`; read
   `/metrics` for `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` before/after the
   window (only meaningful if the process is the same), else count the
   throttled `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning lines (undercounts).
7. **Verdict + evidence.** GREEN if the summed router:500 is 0; RED otherwise
   (AC4). Write the comment, the docs section, and the JSON sidecar.

**Optional tightening (producer's call, not required by AC1):** if the deploy
anchor falls near a 00:00Z rotation boundary, aligning the window to
`<date>T00:00Z → <date+1>T00:00Z` makes it exactly one rotated file, so the
count is exact in **both** directions instead of a bounded superset. Record
which anchoring was used.

**Restart attribution marker.** `proxy/proxy/server.py:754` logs
`Starting LLama Proxy Server` on every start, so the window can be verified
restart-free by grepping the in-window `proxy.log*` files for that marker
(zero hits = no restart inside the window).

## Constraints

- **Read-only measurement:** no restart, no config change, no code change
  (beyond docs/evidence) during the window.
- Window must be restart-free; if a restart happens inside it, restart the
  measurement or report the counter delta as unavailable (AC3).
- Serialise behind the fix: do not start the window while the fix is only in a
  worktree.
- Do not re-run the fix's own verification from here; this item measures only.

## Out of scope / non-goals

- Router `/slots` **400** sign-off — owned by LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8 (its window
  may share the same file set; if it does, record both counts in the same
  comment to avoid a duplicate pass).
- `/health` latency improvement under prefill (context only; file separately
  if it becomes a goal).
- Any further `/slots` call-site fixes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — the only analysis tool; produces the
  router/child responder split (`--summary`, `--json`).
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` — add the dated post-fix window section; update
  the "Target signal going forward" paragraph (AC6).
- `docs/dev/router-slots-500-window-<start>-to-<end>.json` — new evidence
  sidecar, following the shape of
  `docs/dev/router-slots-500-window-2026-10-27-to-28.json`.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `_probe_backend_reachable()` (read-only
  reference: confirms the deployed probe list).
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server*.log*`, `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`
  — inputs (read-only).
- `http://localhost:8000/metrics` — fallback counter (read-only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption A1 — "production" = `main` + restart.** The deployed proxy runs
  from the `main` checkout (`/proc/<pid>/cwd` → `.../projects/llm/proxy`), so
  the deploy anchor is the restart after the `dev → main` promotion, not a
  `dev`-checkout restart.
- **Assumption A2 — superset scoping is acceptable evidence** (AC1): the recipe
  predates this item and is explicitly named in the description; a zero count
  over the ±12 h superset proves zero in-window. A non-zero count is bounded,
  not localised — hence AC4 forces RED rather than an attribution exercise.
  The rotation-aligned anchoring above removes the ambiguity if the timing
  allows.
- **Assumption A3 — the defect is live now**, so a GREEN window can only come
  after a genuine deploy; the intake-time baseline (604 router 500s today) is
  the before-state to quote.
- **Risk R1 — deploy slips.** The fix is uncommitted WIP; if it changes shape
  (e.g. probes the discovered child port instead of dropping `/slots`), the
  expected zero still holds but the "no router /slots request" claim should be
  re-checked against the deployed diff. Mitigation: verify with 3 `/health`
  curls against the new process before opening the window (same live repro as
  above; expect **no** new router `/slots` lines).
- **Risk R2 — in-window restart** (this host restarted the proxy at 10:35Z and
  23:10Z today). Mitigation: AC3 records pid/`lstart` and the counter delta
  requirement; a restart invalidates the delta, not the file-based count.
- **Risk R3 — log retention.** `.gz` rotation gives roughly a week of
  `llama-server` files; measure promptly after the window closes or the files
  age out. Mitigation: run within ~3 days of window end.
- **Risk R4 — coexistence** with the `/slots` 400 window (LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8)
  re-reading the same file set: duplicate cost, not correctness. Mitigation:
  share one parse pass, record both counts.
- **Scope-creep risk:** investigating a non-zero residual beyond filing the bug
  (AC4) belongs in that bug, not here.

## Blocking relationship

`depends-on LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0` (already wired). This item must not be
scheduled for execution until the fix is deployed; intake/planning can proceed.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0** — the fix under test (`/health` probe no longer polls
  router `/slots?model=`). Status `open` / `plan_complete`, WIP in worktree.
- **LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57** — the previous 24 h window measurement whose recipe
  and evidence format this item reuses; its verdict was **RED**: 1,171
  router-responder 500s in the 48 h superset, all attributed to the `/health`
  probe (which became LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0).
- **LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF** — original residual-router-500 bug (child-port
  discovery + call-site fixes; completed).
- **LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8** — sibling post-deploy verification for the `/slots`
  **400** count; shares the measurement recipe and possibly the file set.
- **LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K** — chat-model child-port fallback (`gpt120`) surfaced
  by the same window; affects the fallback-signal reading.
- **LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8** — router `/slots` 400 root cause (`?model=`
  resolution).
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`, `docs/dev/router-slots-500-window-2026-10-27-to-28.json`
  — recipe and evidence-format precedent.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0** – Proxy /health reachability probe polls router GET /slots?model= — residual router-responder /slots 500s under prefill (open)
- **LP-0MPOL5S7W007GRWB** – Include router model in slot save/restore requests (completed)
- **LP-0MPY3DGGF0042178** – proxyctl: restart command (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 0mvp7525p008rxmf, 500s, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+122 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+116 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+116 more)

> Automated keywording: only `proxy/README.md` is relevant; the `ds4/...`
> prompt datasets match on generic AC tokens and are not related to this
> measurement item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Recorded at intake on 2026-10-30 (author: `Map`). The seed context and the
recorded recipe answered all high-signal questions by repo/work-item search;
the three remaining measurement-design questions were settled as documented
assumptions so the item can be planned, and are flagged here for producer
override (none blocks intake or planning).

- **Q1 — Which window anchoring: superset file set (documented recipe) or a
  rotation-aligned exact single-file window?**
  **Recommended:** rotation-aligned when the deploy anchor falls near a 00:00Z
  boundary — it makes the count exact in both directions.
  **Answer (assumed, A2/Method §"Optional tightening"):** AC1 accepts the
  documented superset recipe; rotation alignment is optional and must be
  recorded when used. Source: `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`
  §"Post-fix 24 h window verification" (the description explicitly says to
  reuse that recipe) + §"Limitations".
- **Q2 — What counts as "the fix reaches production"?**
  **Recommended:** merged to `main` **and** the proxy restarted onto that
  build.
  **Answer (assumed, A1):** the deployed proxy runs from the `main` checkout,
  so the deploy anchor is the `/skill:start-proxy --restart` after the
  `dev → main` promotion. Source: `/proc/3797968/cwd` →
  `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy`; the `ship` skill's
  `merge-dev-to-main.sh` (`dev → main` promotion); `proxy/README.md`.
- **Q3 — If the router:500 count is non-zero, may it be attributed (AMBER) or
  must it be RED?**
  **Recommended:** RED, per AC4 as written.
  **Answer (assumed, A2):** non-zero ⇒ RED + linked bug; attribution analysis
  belongs in the linked bug. Source: this item's AC4; predecessor verdict
  discipline in `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`.
- **Research summary:** the recipe, its limitations (timestamp-free
  `llama-server` lines ⇒ ±12 h superset; throttled fallback warnings ⇒
  undercount; counter delta only valid on a restart-free window) and the
  evidence format are all recorded from the 2026-10-27→28 run. The fix itself
  is uncommitted WIP in worktree
  `wl-LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0-proxy-health-reachability-probe-polls-ro`, and the
  live defect reproduced in 3 `/health` calls (2 × router 500).
